Definition: A pair of glasses used to correct or assist defective eyesight.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈspɛk.tə.kəl z/ (Noun, Plural).
Textbook Context: Today our papa is searching everywhere for his spectacles, his only pair!
Memory Trigger: 'SPEC-tacles' help you 'INSPECT' the world clearly!
Visual Icon: A pair of round reading glasses with black frames resting on an open book.

Definition: Looked quickly or briefly at something.
Phonetic & Usage: /ɡlɑːnst/ (Verb, Past Tense).
Textbook Context: He glanced under his wooden chair while searching the room.
Memory Trigger: 'Glanced' is a quick glance or peek!
Visual Icon: A side-profile drawing of an eye looking down quickly at a chair.

Definition: Small pouches sewn into or on clothing for carrying items.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈpɒk.ɪts/ (Noun, Plural).
Textbook Context: He checked inside all his coat pockets for his missing glasses.
Memory Trigger: Pockets carry possessions in your pants or coat!
Visual Icon: A coat jacket showing open side pockets with stitching.

Definition: Looked thoroughly in order to find something.
Phonetic & Usage: /sɜːtʃt/ (Verb, Past Tense).
Textbook Context: Papa searched near the window and across the living room.
Memory Trigger: Search means to seek until you find!
Visual Icon: A magnifying glass held over a room floor layout.

Definition: In or to all places.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɛv.ri.wɛər/ (Adverb / Noun).
Textbook Context: Our papa is searching everywhere in the house today.
Memory Trigger: Everywhere = Every single spot!
Visual Icon: A globe or compass pointing in four directions around a house icon.

Definition: Feeling or showing worry, nervousness, or unease.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈæŋk.ʃəs/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Papa felt anxious when he could not read his morning newspaper.
Memory Trigger: Anxious = Anxiously anticipating answers!
Visual Icon: A face expression showing raised eyebrows and a worried wavy mouth.

Definition: Put in an unremembered or wrong place; temporarily lost.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˌmɪsˈpleɪst/ (Verb, Past Participle).
Textbook Context: He misplaced his only pair of reading glasses during his morning routine.
Memory Trigger: 'MIS-placed' means placed in the WRONG spot!
Visual Icon: A question mark hovering over an empty tabletop.

Definition: Wild or distraught with fear, anxiety, or excitement.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈfræn.tɪk/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Papa made a frantic search across every room in the house.
Memory Trigger: Frantic = Flying frantically around in panic!
Visual Icon: A stylized figure running back and forth with motion blur lines.

Definition: Quick to notice or perceive things in one's environment.
Phonetic & Usage: /əbˈzɜː.vənt/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The observant child noticed the glasses perched on Papa's forehead.
Memory Trigger: Observant eyes observe every detail!
Visual Icon: An owl or child eyes looking through a magnifying glass with a lightbulb above.

Definition: The part of the face above the eyebrows and below the hairline.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈfɒr.ɪd/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Papa's spectacles were resting right there on his forehead!
Memory Trigger: Forehead = Front head above your eyes!
Visual Icon: A line-art face profile highlighting the forehead region with glasses perched on top.

Definition: Things of little value or importance; minor details.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈtraɪ.fəlz/ (Noun, Plural).
Textbook Context: We should not get distressed over minor domestic trifles.
Memory Trigger: Trifles are tiny trivial things!
Visual Icon: A collection of small buttons, pins, and trinkets.

Definition: A feeling of reassurance and relaxation following release from anxiety.
Phonetic & Usage: /rɪˈliːf/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Laughter brought immense relief when the glasses were finally discovered.
Memory Trigger: Relief = Releasing a sigh of comfort!
Visual Icon: A smiling face with a soft exhale wind icon.

Definition: Synonym for glanced: Peeked, glimpsed, or scanned.
Phonetic & Usage: /ɡlɑːnst/ (Verb).
Textbook Context: Papa glanced (peeked) under the desk.
Memory Trigger: Glanced and peeked both mean quick looks!
Visual Icon: Two eyes peeking over a wall.

Definition: Antonym for glanced: Stared, gazed, or glared.
Phonetic & Usage: /ɡlɑːnst/ (Verb).
Textbook Context: Instead of glancing briefly, he stared intently.
Memory Trigger: Stare = Long look vs Glance = Quick look!
Visual Icon: An eye with wide open eyelids gazing continuously.

Definition: Synonym for frantic: Panicked, distraught, or frenzied.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈfræn.tɪk/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: He made a frantic (panicked) search.
Memory Trigger: Frantic and panicked describe wild worry!
Visual Icon: Exclamation marks around a running figure.

Definition: Antonym for frantic: Calm, relaxed, or serene.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈfræn.tɪk/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The child remained calm while Papa was frantic.
Memory Trigger: Calm keeps cool under pressure!
Visual Icon: A peaceful lotus or calm resting water droplet.

Definition: Antonym for misplaced: Found, located, or recovered.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˌmɪsˈpleɪst/ (Verb).
Textbook Context: The misplaced item was quickly found.
Memory Trigger: Lost vs Found - opposites in finding things!
Visual Icon: A checkmark inside a circle over a found key.

Definition: Antonym for near: Far, distant, or remote.
Phonetic & Usage: /nɪər/ (Preposition / Adjective).
Textbook Context: He searched near the window and far across the hall.
Memory Trigger: Near is close; Far is distant!
Visual Icon: Two dots - one close to a box, one far away.

Definition: Antonym for clean: Dirty, soiled, or messy.
Phonetic & Usage: /kliːn/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Keep your study table clean rather than dirty.
Memory Trigger: Clean shines; Dirty needs washing!
Visual Icon: A sparkling clean plate beside a smudged dirt plate.

Definition: Antonym for bright: Dark, dim, or gloomy.
Phonetic & Usage: /braɪt/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The bright sun lit up the dark corner.
Memory Trigger: Bright shines light; Dark lacks light!
Visual Icon: A glowing sun half-split with a dark crescent moon.

Definition: Antonym for honest: Deceitful, dishonest, or untruthful.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɒn.ɪst/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Always be honest rather than deceitful.
Memory Trigger: Honest tells truth; Deceitful hides it!
Visual Icon: A scale of justice balanced with a heart.

Definition: Antonym for careless: Careful, attentive, or cautious.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈkɛə.ləs/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Do not be careless with glasses; be careful!
Memory Trigger: Careless loses things; Careful keeps them safe!
Visual Icon: A pair of hands gently cradling an egg.

Definition: The letter 'k' is silent when followed by 'n' at the start of a word.
Phonetic & Usage: /neʊ/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: We know that Papa misplaced his spectacles.
Memory Trigger: When K meets N at the start, K stays quiet!
Visual Icon: A letter K with a small mute speaker icon next to letter N.

Definition: The letter 'w' is silent before 'r' at the start of words.
Phonetic & Usage: /raɪt/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Write down the poem in story format.
Memory Trigger: W is silent before R in write!
Visual Icon: A pencil writing 'Write' with the 'W' faded in grey.

Definition: The past tense suffix '-ed' sounds like '/t/' after voiceless consonants like 'c' (/s/).
Phonetic & Usage: /ɡlɑːnst/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: He glanced (/glɑːnst/) under his chair.
Memory Trigger: Glanced ends with a crisp /t/ sound!
Visual Icon: A speaker box showing 'glanced' -> /t/ sound wave.

Definition: Words with three syllables like 'spec-ta-cles' have primary stress on the first syllable.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈspɛk.tə.kəl z/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Say 'SPEC-ta-cles' with emphasis on SPEC.
Memory Trigger: Break it: SPEC - TA - CLES!
Visual Icon: Three sound blocks with the first block highlighted larger.

Definition: The letter 'b' is silent when it comes after 'm' at the end of a word.
Phonetic & Usage: /koʊm/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Papa used a comb before searching for his glasses.
Memory Trigger: M silences B at the end of a word!
Visual Icon: A hair comb with a ghosted silent letter 'B'.

Definition: The letter 'g' is silent when followed by 'n' at the beginning of a word.
Phonetic & Usage: /næt/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: A tiny gnat flew near the windowpane.
Memory Trigger: G is quiet before N in gnat!
Visual Icon: A tiny insect with a silent 'G' crossed out gently.

Definition: The second 'c' in spectacles followed by 'l' makes a hard /k/ sound, while before 'e' it makes soft /s/.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈspɛk.tə.kəl z/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Spectacles has both hard and soft consonant blends.
Memory Trigger: C before E says /s/; C before L says /k/!
Visual Icon: A phonetic chart showing 'c' sound branches.

Definition: The letter 't' is often silent in words ending with '-ften'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɒf.ən/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Papa often misplaces his small daily items.
Memory Trigger: T sleeps in 'often'!
Visual Icon: A clock face with a muted 'T' icon.

Definition: Words that show the physical position or location of a noun (under, inside, on, near).
Phonetic & Usage: Preposition Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Inside his pockets, under his chair, near the window, on his head.
Memory Trigger: Prepositions position things in space!
Visual Icon: Four spatial boxes showing 'in', 'on', 'under', and 'near'.

Definition: Shortened forms of verbs combined with 'not' using an apostrophe (can't, isn't, hasn't).
Phonetic & Usage: Contraction Rule (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: He can't read the paper; he can't watch TV.
Memory Trigger: An apostrophe replaces missing letters in contractions!
Visual Icon: Two puzzle pieces 'can' + 'not' locking into 'can't'.

Definition: A phrase used to quantify items that consist of two matching parts (a pair of glasses/shoes).
Phonetic & Usage: Noun Phrase (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: He lost his spectacles, his only pair!
Memory Trigger: A pair means TWO matching things working as ONE!
Visual Icon: Two shoes connected by an equal sign = a pair.

Definition: Sentences that ask a question and end with a question mark.
Phonetic & Usage: Sentence Type (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Oh! Where can it be? Where are my glasses?
Memory Trigger: Questions ask for answers and end with '?'!
Visual Icon: A giant question mark over a dialogue bubble.

Definition: Sentences expressing strong emotion or surprise ending with an exclamation mark.
Phonetic & Usage: Sentence Type (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Stop, Papa! It is right there on your head!
Memory Trigger: Exclamations shout or express excitement with '!'!
Visual Icon: An exclamation mark inside a starburst shape.

Definition: Nouns like 'spectacles', 'scissors', and 'trousers' that are always used in plural form.
Phonetic & Usage: Noun Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Spectacles are always plural because they have two lenses.
Memory Trigger: Two parts make one plural noun item!
Visual Icon: Icons of spectacles, scissors, and pants grouped together.

Definition: Verbs describing actions completed in past time (checked, glanced, searched, looked).
Phonetic & Usage: Verb Tense (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: He checked inside his pockets and looked under his chair.
Memory Trigger: Past verbs tell what ALREADY happened!
Visual Icon: A timeline arrow pointing backwards into past events.

Definition: Adding 's to a noun to show ownership or belonging (Papa's spectacles).
Phonetic & Usage: Punctuation Rule (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Papa's spectacles belong to Papa.
Memory Trigger: Apostrophe 's shows WHO owns the item!
Visual Icon: A label tag showing 'Papa's' attached to glasses.

Definition: Can't is the shortened contraction for 'cannot'.
Phonetic & Usage: /kɑːnt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: He can't read the newspaper without his glasses.
Memory Trigger: Can't = Can + Not!
Visual Icon: A red 'NO' circle over the word 'CAN'.

Definition: Where's is the contraction for 'where is'.
Phonetic & Usage: /wɛəz/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: Where's my pair of reading spectacles?
Memory Trigger: Where's asks where something IS!
Visual Icon: A magnifying glass searching over a location pin.

Definition: He's stands for 'he is' or 'he has'.
Phonetic & Usage: /hiːz/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: He's searching everywhere in the house.
Memory Trigger: He's = He + Is!
Visual Icon: A boy icon pointing to himself.

Definition: It's is the contraction for 'it is'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ɪts/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: It's resting right there on your forehead!
Memory Trigger: It's = It + Is!
Visual Icon: A finger pointing to an object.

Definition: Doesn't is the contraction for 'does not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈdʌz.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: He doesn't realize the glasses are on his head.
Memory Trigger: Doesn't = Does + Not!
Visual Icon: A crossing-out gesture icon.

Definition: Wouldn't is the contraction for 'would not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈwʊd.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: He wouldn't give up searching until he found them.
Memory Trigger: Wouldn't = Would + Not!
Visual Icon: A shield showing a refusal gesture.

Definition: Clearly visible without any concealment, yet remaining unnoticed.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The missing glasses were resting in plain sight on his head.
Memory Trigger: In plain sight = Openly visible right before your eyes!
Visual Icon: An eye looking directly at an open pedestal.

Definition: Two corresponding or matching things used together.
Phonetic & Usage: Quantitative Phrase (Phrase).
Textbook Context: He lost his spectacles, his only pair.
Memory Trigger: A pair of = Two matching items!
Visual Icon: A set of twin boots side by side.

Definition: Search thoroughly everywhere in all possible places.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Papa searched high and low across the living room.
Memory Trigger: High and low = Up in cupboards and down under chairs!
Visual Icon: An arrow pointing UP to a shelf and DOWN under a table.

Definition: Cause great disorder in a place while searching thoroughly.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: He turned the house upside down looking for his glasses.
Memory Trigger: Upside down = Flipping everything over!
Visual Icon: A house icon turned completely upside down.

Definition: Located directly on top of one's forehead or hair.
Phonetic & Usage: Prepositional Phrase (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Your spectacles are right there on your head!
Memory Trigger: Right on your head = Touching your forehead!
Visual Icon: A smile cartoon with glasses resting on its forehead.

Definition: Become angry or frustrated when unable to find something.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Papa stayed patient and did not lose his temper.
Memory Trigger: Keep calm and don't blow your top!
Visual Icon: A steam puff icon coming out of a kettle.

flashcards.back_content:
Definition: Maneuver a ball with short, controlled taps using a stick or foot.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈdrɪb.əl/ (Verb / Noun).
Textbook Context: Jay taught Gopi how to dribble the hockey ball across the field.
Memory Trigger: Dribble = Dabbing the ball gently down the field!
Visual Icon: A hockey stick tapping a small white ball in short dashes.

Definition: A soft, dry sound made by dry leaves, paper, or silk moving together.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈrʌs.əl/ (Noun / Verb).
Textbook Context: Gopi heard a soft rustle among the dry leaves in his yard.
Memory Trigger: Leaves rustle when wind blows through them!
Visual Icon: Autumn leaves tumbling in wind with sound motion waves.

Definition: Grasped or took hold of something suddenly or eagerly.
Phonetic & Usage: /ɡræbd/ (Verb, Past Tense).
Textbook Context: He grabbed his wooden hockey stick and ran out to play.
Memory Trigger: Grabbed = Snatched up quickly!
Visual Icon: A hand gripping a wooden sports handle firmly.

Definition: A dull, heavy sound such as that made by an object falling to earth.
Phonetic & Usage: /θʌd/ (Noun / Onomatopoeia).
Textbook Context: The ball hit the ground with a loud thud.
Memory Trigger: Thud is the heavy sound of a bump!
Visual Icon: A ball bouncing off ground with an impact star graphic.

Definition: Having no knowledge of a situation or fact; oblivious.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˌʌn.əˈwɛər/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The scooter driver was completely unaware of his new passenger.
Memory Trigger: UN-aware = NOT aware!
Visual Icon: A driver riding forward with a question mark behind his back.

Definition: A remarkable concurrence of events without apparent causal connection.
Phonetic & Usage: /koʊˈɪn.sɪ.dəns/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: It was a hilarious coincidence that the ball landed in the basket.
Memory Trigger: Coincidence = Co-occurring by chance!
Visual Icon: Two intersecting puzzle pieces coming together by accident.

Definition: A container used to hold or carry things, mounted on a vehicle.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈbɑː.skɪt/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The hockey ball landed right inside the front basket of the scooter.
Memory Trigger: Baskets hold things securely!
Visual Icon: A woven wire basket attached to the front handlebars of a scooter.

Definition: A line or border that marks the limits of an area or playing field.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈbaʊn.dər.i/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Jay struck the ball so hard it cleared the field boundary.
Memory Trigger: Boundary bounds the playground limits!
Visual Icon: A dotted fence line enclosing a green sports turf.

Definition: A light two-wheeled motor vehicle with a step-through frame.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈskuː.tər/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The scooter sped down the street carrying the ball away.
Memory Trigger: Scooter scoots fast down the road!
Visual Icon: A colorful motor scooter with handlebars and wheels.

Definition: Fair, generous, and polite behavior during a sports game.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈspɔːts.mən.ʃɪp/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The children showed great sportsmanship by laughing at the accident.
Memory Trigger: Sportsmanship makes sports fun for all!
Visual Icon: Two hands shaking across a field boundary.

Definition: The rate of change of velocity; speeding up.
Phonetic & Usage: /əkˌsɛl.əˈreɪ.ʃən/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The scooter's sudden acceleration carried the ball out of reach.
Memory Trigger: Accelerate = Go faster and faster!
Visual Icon: A speedometer gauge needle sweeping to the right.

Definition: A narrow way, path, or corridor allowing travel.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈpæs.ɪdʒ/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The scooter drove along the narrow village passage.
Memory Trigger: Passage is a path to pass through!
Visual Icon: A paved path between two village garden walls.

Definition: Synonym for rustle: Crackle, swish, or rustling sound.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈrʌs.əl/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: He heard a soft rustle (crackle) among the leaves.
Memory Trigger: Rustle and crackle both mean dry leaf sounds!
Visual Icon: Dry leaves blowing across grass.

Definition: Antonym for unaware: Aware, conscious, or mindful.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˌʌn.əˈwɛər/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: He was aware of the rules of the game.
Memory Trigger: Aware knows; Unaware does not know!
Visual Icon: An eye opening wide in recognition.

Definition: Antonym for grabbed: Released, dropped, or let go.
Phonetic & Usage: /ɡræbd/ (Verb).
Textbook Context: He released his grip on the stick.
Memory Trigger: Grab holds tight; Release lets go!
Visual Icon: An open palm releasing a ball.

Definition: Antonym for fast: Slow, sluggish, or gradual.
Phonetic & Usage: /fɑːst/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The scooter was fast, but the turtle was slow.
Memory Trigger: Fast moves quick; Slow takes time!
Visual Icon: A hare running next to a slow tortoise.

Definition: Antonym for loud: Quiet, silent, or muted.
Phonetic & Usage: /laʊd/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The thud was loud, but the rustle was quiet.
Memory Trigger: Loud makes noise; Quiet stays silent!
Visual Icon: A booming speaker next to a muted volume icon.

Definition: Antonym for smooth: Rough, bumpy, or uneven.
Phonetic & Usage: /smuːð/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The turf was smooth, but the dirt path was rough.
Memory Trigger: Smooth is level; Rough has bumps!
Visual Icon: A flat glass surface next to a jagged rock.

Definition: Antonym for win: Lose, forfeit, or suffer defeat.
Phonetic & Usage: /wɪn/ (Verb).
Textbook Context: Both teams play fair whether they win or lose.
Memory Trigger: Win takes trophy; Lose learns for next time!
Visual Icon: A winner trophy cup beside a silver runner-up ribbon.

Definition: Antonym for joyful: Sorrowful, sad, or gloomy.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈdʒɔɪ.fəl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The children had a joyful match rather than a gloomy one.
Memory Trigger: Joyful smiles; Sorrowful frowns!
Visual Icon: A bright sun face next to a rainy cloud face.

Definition: Antonym for friends: Foes, enemies, or rivals.
Phonetic & Usage: /frɛndz/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Play with your friends and treat rivals with respect.
Memory Trigger: Friends share joy; Foes compete fiercely!
Visual Icon: Two smiling pals hugging.

Definition: Synonym for boundary: Border, perimeter, or limit.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈbaʊn.dər.i/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The ball crossed the boundary (border) line.
Memory Trigger: Boundary and border define the perimeter!
Visual Icon: A red fence line around a park.

Definition: The letter 't' is silent in words ending in '-stle' like rustle, whistle, castle.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈrʌs.əl/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Listen to the leaves rustle (/rʌs.əl/) in the breeze.
Memory Trigger: T stays quiet when leaves rustle!
Visual Icon: A whistle with the letter 'T' crossed out in grey.

Definition: The letter 'w' is silent before 'r' in words like wrist, write, wrong.
Phonetic & Usage: /rɪst/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Jay flicked his wrist to strike the ball.
Memory Trigger: W rests when WR start a word!
Visual Icon: A wrist watch with a ghosted silent letter 'W'.

Definition: The double vowel 'oo' makes a long /uː/ sound in scooter, moon, spoon.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈskuː.tər/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The scooter (/skuː.tər/) zoomed down the lane.
Memory Trigger: Double OO says /uː/ like zoom!
Visual Icon: Two 'O's forming wheels of a scooter.

Definition: The letter cluster '-gh-' makes an /f/ sound in words like laughter, laugh, rough.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈlɑːf.tər/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The children burst into laughter (/lɑːf.tər/).
Memory Trigger: GH in laugh sounds like F!
Visual Icon: A laughing face with 'GH -> /f/' sound bubble.

Definition: The letter 'k' is silent before 'n' in knock, knee, knife.
Phonetic & Usage: /nɒk/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: He heard a knock at the playgate.
Memory Trigger: K is silent before N!
Visual Icon: A hand knocking on a door with a muted 'K'.

Definition: The letter 'l' is silent before 'f' or 'm' in half, calf, palm, talk.
Phonetic & Usage: /hɑːf/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Half the team chased the ball.
Memory Trigger: L drops out in half!
Visual Icon: A circle cut in two halves with silent 'L' crossed out.

Definition: The letter 'g' followed by 'r' makes a hard /ɡ/ sound as in grabbed, green, great.
Phonetic & Usage: /ɡræbd/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Gopi grabbed (/ɡræbd/) the stick quickly.
Memory Trigger: G before R says hard /g/!
Visual Icon: A fist gripping a stick with sound waves.

Definition: The letter 'c' before 'i' or 'e' makes a soft /s/ sound as in coincidence, city, ice.
Phonetic & Usage: /koʊˈɪn.sɪ.dəns/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: What a hilarious coincidence (/s/)!
Memory Trigger: C before I says soft /s/!
Visual Icon: A phonetic snake 'S' icon over letter C.

Definition: Words that tell how often an action happens (always, usually, sometimes, rarely, never).
Phonetic & Usage: Adverb Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Jay always practices dribbling; they rarely lose a ball.
Memory Trigger: Adverbs of frequency show HOW OFTEN!
Visual Icon: A dial meter from 0% (never) to 100% (always).

Definition: Verbs expressing physical movement completed in past time (dribbled, bounced, zoomed).
Phonetic & Usage: Verb Tense (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: The ball bounced high and zoomed into the basket.
Memory Trigger: Dynamic verbs move fast in the past!
Visual Icon: An arrow bouncing over obstacles.

Definition: Words showing motion toward or across a space (into, across, over, through).
Phonetic & Usage: Preposition Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: It flew over the fence and into the scooter basket.
Memory Trigger: Prepositions of movement show WHERE things flow!
Visual Icon: An arching arrow leaping OVER a fence into a bowl.

Definition: Specific names of particular people, places, or things requiring capital letters (Gopi, Jay).
Phonetic & Usage: Noun Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Gopi and Jay played hockey together.
Memory Trigger: Proper names ALWAYS start with a CAPITAL letter!
Visual Icon: Name tags showing 'Gopi' and 'Jay' with big capitals.

Definition: Nouns representing intangible ideas, qualities, or feelings rather than physical objects.
Phonetic & Usage: Noun Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Sportsmanship means enjoying games fairly.
Memory Trigger: You can't touch an abstract noun, but you feel it!
Visual Icon: A brain and heart icon connected by light rays.

Definition: Nouns formed by combining two smaller words together (play + ground = playground).
Phonetic & Usage: Word Formation (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: They gathered on the village playground.
Memory Trigger: Two small words join to make ONE compound noun!
Visual Icon: Puzzle piece 'Play' + 'Ground' = 'Playground'.

Definition: Sentences expressing strong excitement or surprise ending with an exclamation point.
Phonetic & Usage: Sentence Type (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: What a hit! Look at the ball go!
Memory Trigger: Exclamations shout out with '!'!
Visual Icon: A starburst speech bubble with 'What a hit!'

Definition: Contrasting ongoing present actions (is riding) with completed past events (drove away).
Phonetic & Usage: Tense Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: The driver is riding now, but the ball bounced earlier.
Memory Trigger: Present = NOW; Past = THEN!
Visual Icon: A split screen clock showing 'Now' and 'Yesterday'.

Definition: Couldn't is the contraction for 'could not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈkʊd.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: They couldn't stop laughing at the scooter.
Memory Trigger: Couldn't = Could + Not!
Visual Icon: A red X over a running figure.

Definition: Didn't is the contraction for 'did not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈdɪd.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: The driver didn't notice the ball in his basket.
Memory Trigger: Didn't = Did + Not!
Visual Icon: A hand shaking 'no'.

Definition: They're is the contraction for 'they are'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ðɛər/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: They're playing hockey on the green playground.
Memory Trigger: They're = They + Are!
Visual Icon: A group of children standing together.

Definition: We'll is the contraction for 'we will'.
Phonetic & Usage: /wiːl/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: We'll find another ball to finish our game.
Memory Trigger: We'll = We + Will!
Visual Icon: A team placing hands in a central pledge.

Definition: Wasn't is the contraction for 'was not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈwɒz.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: It wasn't intentional, but it was hilarious!
Memory Trigger: Wasn't = Was + Not!
Visual Icon: A past calendar page with an X.

Definition: Let's is the contraction for 'let us'.
Phonetic & Usage: /lɛts/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: Let's start the match before sunset!
Memory Trigger: Let's = Let + Us!
Visual Icon: An encouraging gesture pointing forward.

Definition: Disappeared extremely quickly in a split second.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The scooter and the ball were gone in a flash!
Memory Trigger: Gone in a flash = Fast as lighting!
Visual Icon: A lightning bolt icon with speed lines.

Definition: Suddenly start laughing out loud loudly and uncontrollably.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: All the children burst into laughter when the scooter sped away.
Memory Trigger: Burst into laughter = Laughter exploding like fireworks!
Visual Icon: A laughing emoji with tears of joy.

Definition: Hit a ball completely outside the field limit line.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Jay's powerful hit cleared the playground boundary.
Memory Trigger: Clear the boundary = Over the line!
Visual Icon: A ball soaring over a boundary fence.

Definition: Appearing unexpectedly as if from nowhere.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The rustling sound seemed to come out of thin air.
Memory Trigger: Out of thin air = Popping up like magic!
Visual Icon: A magician's hat with a ball floating up.

Definition: Operating at the highest level of activity or momentum.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The hockey match was in full swing when the ball flew out.
Memory Trigger: In full swing = Moving at top momentum!
Visual Icon: A pendulum or stick swinging at full arc.

Definition: Become so absorbed in an activity that one forgets the time.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: They lost track of time while playing in the yard.
Memory Trigger: Lose track of time = Clock ticks by unnoticed!
Visual Icon: A clock face fading into fun sports icons.

flashcards.back_content:
Definition: Move smoothly over water or through the air.
Phonetic & Usage: /seɪl/ (Verb / Noun).
Textbook Context: Boats sail on the rivers, and ships sail on the seas.
Memory Trigger: Sail glides smoothly like a sailboat!
Visual Icon: A sailboat riding blue ocean waves.

Definition: The land surface of the world or our planet.
Phonetic & Usage: /ɜːθ/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The rainbow builds a road from earth to sky.
Memory Trigger: Earth is the ground beneath our feet!
Visual Icon: A green landscape under a blue sky.

Definition: The sky or realm above the earth.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈhɛv.ən/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The rainbow is the bow that bridges heaven over the trees.
Memory Trigger: Heaven is high above the treetops!
Visual Icon: White fluffy clouds floating in deep sky blue.

Definition: Rises above or towers over the top of something.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˌoʊ.vərˈtɒps/ (Verb).
Textbook Context: The rainbow overtops the highest forest trees.
Memory Trigger: OVER-tops means towering OVER the top!
Visual Icon: A rainbow arch soaring above tall pine trees.

Definition: An arch of colors formed in the sky by the refraction of sunlight through raindrops.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈreɪn.boʊ/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Clouds are pretty, but the rainbow is prettier far than these.
Memory Trigger: Rain + Bow = Rainbow!
Visual Icon: A 7-colored curved arc stretching across clouds.

Definition: A transparent glass object that refracts white light into a spectrum of colors.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈprɪz.əm/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Raindrops act as tiny prisms in the atmosphere.
Memory Trigger: Prisms split light into VIBGYOR colors!
Visual Icon: A triangular glass prism refracting light into 7 rays.

Definition: The bending of light rays as they pass from one medium into another.
Phonetic & Usage: /rɪˈfræk.ʃən/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Refraction of sunlight in water drops creates rainbows.
Memory Trigger: Refraction bends light rays!
Visual Icon: A light beam bending as it enters a water drop.

Definition: Acronym for Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈvɪb.ɡjɔːr/ (Acronym / Noun).
Textbook Context: The 7 colors of the rainbow follow the VIBGYOR sequence.
Memory Trigger: VIBGYOR = Violet to Red rainbow order!
Visual Icon: A color wheel showing 7 spectrum slices.

Definition: A structure carrying a pathway over an obstacle like a river.
Phonetic & Usage: /brɪdʒ/ (Noun / Verb).
Textbook Context: There are bridges on the rivers, as pretty as you please.
Memory Trigger: Bridges connect two sides over water!
Visual Icon: A stone arch bridge spanning a flowing river.

Definition: Made or constructed by human beings rather than nature.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈmæn.meɪd/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Ships and stone bridges are man-made structures.
Memory Trigger: Man-made = Built by people!
Visual Icon: A crane building a bridge next to trees.

Definition: Vehicles designed for travel on water (boats, ships).
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈwɔː.tər.krɑːft/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Boats and ships are traditional watercraft.
Memory Trigger: Watercraft craft their way on water!
Visual Icon: A small rowboat beside an ocean ship.

Definition: Existing in or caused by nature; not artificial.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈnætʃ.ər.əl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The rainbow is nature's most beautiful natural wonder.
Memory Trigger: Natural comes from Mother Nature!
Visual Icon: A serene forest waterfall under a rainbow.

Definition: Synonym for pretty: Lovely, attractive, or beautiful.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈprɪt.i/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The river bridges are pretty (lovely) to see.
Memory Trigger: Pretty and lovely describe appealing sights!
Visual Icon: A colorful flower garden in bloom.

Definition: Antonym for prettier: Less attractive or uglier.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈprɪt.i.ər/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Clouds are prettier than boats; boats are less attractive.
Memory Trigger: Prettier wins in visual beauty!
Visual Icon: A bright rainbow next to a plain gray block.

Definition: Antonym for far: Near, close, or adjacent.
Phonetic & Usage: /fɑːr/ (Adjective / Adverb).
Textbook Context: The rainbow reaches far into the sky, not near.
Memory Trigger: Far is distant; Near is close!
Visual Icon: An arrow pointing to a distant mountain.

Definition: Antonym for build: Destroy, demolish, or break.
Phonetic & Usage: /bɪld/ (Verb).
Textbook Context: We build bridges; storm winds demolish them.
Memory Trigger: Build creates; Destroy tears down!
Visual Icon: A house being built with bricks next to a wrecking ball.

Definition: Antonym for heaven: Earth, ground, or underworld.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈhɛv.ən/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The arch links heaven above to earth below.
Memory Trigger: Heaven is sky; Earth is ground!
Visual Icon: Sky clouds above green grass below.

Definition: Antonym for broad: Narrow, thin, or slender.
Phonetic & Usage: /brɔːd/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: A broad rainbow bridges narrow streams.
Memory Trigger: Broad is wide; Narrow is thin!
Visual Icon: A wide highway beside a thin pathway.

Definition: Synonym for bright: Luminous, radiant, or vivid.
Phonetic & Usage: /braɪt/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The rainbow shows bright (vivid) colors.
Memory Trigger: Bright and vivid shine with light!
Visual Icon: A shining sun emitting light rays.

Definition: Antonym for high: Low, sunken, or deep.
Phonetic & Usage: /haɪ/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The clouds sail high while boats float low.
Memory Trigger: High reaches up; Low sits down!
Visual Icon: A mountain peak next to a deep valley.

Definition: Synonym for smooth: Calm, placid, or tranquil.
Phonetic & Usage: /smuːð/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Boats sail on smooth (calm) rivers.
Memory Trigger: Smooth water has no waves!
Visual Icon: A mirror-like lake reflecting trees.

Definition: Antonym for natural: Artificial, synthetic, or man-made.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈnætʃ.ər.əl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Rainbows are natural; bridges are man-made.
Memory Trigger: Natural = Nature; Artificial = Built!
Visual Icon: A wild flower next to a plastic toy flower.

Definition: The letter combination 'gh' is silent in words like high, sky-high, night, light.
Phonetic & Usage: /haɪ/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The rainbow arcs high (/haɪ/) in the sky.
Memory Trigger: GH is quiet in HIGH!
Visual Icon: A mountain peak with silent 'GH' crossed out.

Definition: The letter 'd' is silent before 'ge' in bridge, ridge, edge, judge.
Phonetic & Usage: /brɪdʒ/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The rainbow forms a bridge (/brɪdʒ/) over trees.
Memory Trigger: D goes silent in bridge!
Visual Icon: A stone bridge with a ghosted silent letter 'D'.

Definition: The vowel pair 'ai' makes a long /eɪ/ sound in sail, rain, main, paint.
Phonetic & Usage: /seɪl/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Ships sail (/seɪl/) across the sea.
Memory Trigger: AI says /eɪ/ like day!
Visual Icon: A boat sailing under the word 'SAIL'.

Definition: The vowel pair 'ow' makes an /oʊ/ sound in bow, rainbow, show, grow.
Phonetic & Usage: /boʊ/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The colorful bow (/boʊ/) overtops the trees.
Memory Trigger: OW says /oʊ/ in rainbow!
Visual Icon: A archery bow curving into a rainbow arc.

Definition: When 'y' changes to 'i' in prettier, '-ier' makes an /i.ər/ sound.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈprɪt.i.ər/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Clouds are prettier (/prɪt.i.ər/) than ships.
Memory Trigger: Pretty becomes prettier!
Visual Icon: A comparative chart: Pretty -> Prettier.

Definition: The letter 'w' is silent in sword, answer, two.
Phonetic & Usage: /sɔːd/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The knight held a sword by the bridge.
Memory Trigger: W is silent in sword!
Visual Icon: A steel sword with a muted letter 'W'.

Definition: The letter 'k' is silent before 'n' in knight, know, knee.
Phonetic & Usage: /naɪt/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: A knight crossed the stone bridge.
Memory Trigger: K sleeps before N in knight!
Visual Icon: A helmeted knight with silent 'K'.

Definition: The letter 'b' is silent in doubt, debt, subtle.
Phonetic & Usage: /daʊt/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: There is no doubt that rainbows are beautiful.
Memory Trigger: B stays quiet in doubt!
Visual Icon: A question mark over a silent letter 'B'.

Definition: Adjectives change form to compare nouns: Positive (pretty), Comparative (prettier), Superlative (prettiest).
Phonetic & Usage: Adjective Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Ships are pretty, but clouds are prettier.
Memory Trigger: Pretty -> Prettier -> Prettiest!
Visual Icon: Three steps rising in height: Pretty, Prettier, Prettiest.

Definition: Poetic structure where alternating or paired line endings rhyme (seas/these, please/trees).
Phonetic & Usage: Poetic Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Boats sail on the rivers, and ships sail on the seas / ...prettier than these.
Memory Trigger: ABCB rhyming rhythm creates musical poetry!
Visual Icon: A poem stanza with matching rhyming color highlights.

flashcards.front_content: Prepositions of Direction: Earth to Sky
flashcards.back_content:
Definition: Prepositions showing directional span from a starting point to a destination (from... to).
Phonetic & Usage: Preposition Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Builds a road from earth to sky.
Memory Trigger: From start TO destination!
Visual Icon: An arrow spanning from the ground up to a cloud.

Definition: Forming plurals by adding '-s' or '-es' (boat -> boats, bridge -> bridges, cloud -> clouds).
Phonetic & Usage: Noun Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Boats, ships, rivers, bridges, and clouds.
Memory Trigger: Add -S or -ES to make plurals!
Visual Icon: One boat icon next to three boat icons.

Definition: Comparing two unlike things directly without using 'like' or 'as' (the bow builds a road).
Phonetic & Usage: Literary Device (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: The rainbow builds a road from earth to sky.
Memory Trigger: A metaphor turns a rainbow into a sky road!
Visual Icon: A rainbow painted with yellow highway road lines.

Definition: Using 'than' after comparative adjectives to compare two things (prettier than these).
Phonetic & Usage: Conjunction Rule (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Clouds are prettier THAN ships.
Memory Trigger: Use THAN when comparing TWO things!
Visual Icon: A balance scale comparing clouds and ships.

Definition: Capitalizing names of specific authors and places (Christina Rossetti, Newton).
Phonetic & Usage: Punctuation Rule (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Christina Rossetti wrote 'The Rainbow'.
Memory Trigger: Capitalize author names!
Visual Icon: Name card showing 'Christina Rossetti'.

flashcards.front_content: Action Verbs of Motion: Sail, Build
flashcards.back_content:
Definition: Verbs that describe active movement or creation (sail, overtops, builds).
Phonetic & Usage: Verb Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Clouds sail and the bow builds a road.
Memory Trigger: Motion verbs bring poetry to life!
Visual Icon: A sailboat icon next to a hammer icon.

Definition: There's is the contraction for 'there is'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ðɛəz/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: There's a rainbow soaring above the forest.
Memory Trigger: There's = There + Is!
Visual Icon: A finger pointing to a sky arch.

Definition: What's is the contraction for 'what is'.
Phonetic & Usage: /wɒts/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: What's prettier than a sailing ship?
Memory Trigger: What's = What + Is!
Visual Icon: A question bubble icon.

Definition: Who's is the contraction for 'who is'.
Phonetic & Usage: /huːz/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: Who's looking at the rainbow in the sky?
Memory Trigger: Who's = Who + Is!
Visual Icon: A silhouette figure looking up.

Definition: Isn't is the contraction for 'is not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɪz.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: A stone bridge isn't as colorful as a rainbow.
Memory Trigger: Isn't = Is + Not!
Visual Icon: A red X over an equal sign.

Definition: They've is the contraction for 'they have'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ðeɪv/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: They've built a bridge across the wide river.
Memory Trigger: They've = They + Have!
Visual Icon: A team of construction workers.

Definition: It'll is the contraction for 'it will'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɪt.əl/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: It'll rain before the rainbow appears.
Memory Trigger: It'll = It + Will!
Visual Icon: A rain cloud transitioning to a sun.

Definition: In an ideal, magical, or far-away wonderful place.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Dreams come true over the rainbow.
Memory Trigger: Over the rainbow = A magical place high above!
Visual Icon: A star shining above a rainbow arch.

Definition: Connect two different things or resolve a difference between groups.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The rainbow helps bridge the gap between earth and sky.
Memory Trigger: Bridge the gap = Bring two sides together!
Visual Icon: A bridge connecting two steep cliffs.

Definition: Much more beautiful than all the other options mentioned.
Phonetic & Usage: Poetic Phrase (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The sky bow is prettier far than man-made ships.
Memory Trigger: Prettier far = Much more lovely!
Visual Icon: A sparkling rainbow crowned with stars.

Definition: Spanning the complete distance from the ground up into the heavens.
Phonetic & Usage: Prepositional Phrase (Phrase).
Textbook Context: It builds a road from earth to sky.
Memory Trigger: Earth to sky = Ground to clouds!
Visual Icon: A vertical arrow rising from grass to sky.

Definition: All seven spectral colors (VIBGYOR) displayed together.
Phonetic & Usage: Common Phrase (Phrase).
Textbook Context: She painted her box with the colors of the rainbow.
Memory Trigger: 7 colors in perfect order!
Visual Icon: A palette showing 7 vibrant paint strokes.

Definition: An imagined valuable reward found at the end of a rainbow.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Legend says there is a pot of gold at the rainbow's end.
Memory Trigger: Pot of gold = Ultimate treasure!
Visual Icon: A black pot filled with shining gold coins at a rainbow's base.

flashcards.back_content:
Definition: A person involved in wholesale trade or supplying goods.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈmɜː.tʃənt/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: A wealthy merchant kept a beautiful parrot in a golden cage.
Memory Trigger: Merchants trade goods for money!
Visual Icon: A merchant in traditional attire holding a trade pouch.

Definition: Confined or trapped inside a cage; deprived of freedom.
Phonetic & Usage: /keɪdʒd/ (Adjective / Verb).
Textbook Context: The caged parrot longed to fly freely in the forest.
Memory Trigger: Caged = Trapped behind bars!
Visual Icon: A bird behind golden cage bars looking outward.

Definition: A large area covered chiefly with trees and undergrowth.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈfɒr.ɪst/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The merchant traveled through a dense forest to buy goods.
Memory Trigger: Forest = Thousands of wild trees!
Visual Icon: A dense green woodland with tall trees.

Definition: A protected nature reserve where birds and animals are safe.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈsæŋk.tʃu.ər.i/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: India has famous avian sanctuaries like Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary.
Memory Trigger: Sanctuary = Safe haven for wildlife!
Visual Icon: A park sign with a bird flying safely over water.

Definition: Polite words or messages sent to someone upon arrival or meeting.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɡriː.tɪŋz/ (Noun, Plural).
Textbook Context: The merchant conveyed greetings from the caged bird to its wild friends.
Memory Trigger: Greetings say hello and send love!
Visual Icon: An envelope carrying a dove and message ribbon.

Definition: Pretended or faked a state, feeling, or condition.
Phonetic & Usage: /feɪnd/ (Verb, Past Tense).
Textbook Context: The wild parrot feigned death and dropped from the branch.
Memory Trigger: Feigned = Faked to trick someone!
Visual Icon: A parrot lying still on a branch with one eye peeking.

Definition: The power or right to act, speak, or live without hindrance or restraint.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈfriː.dəm/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Priceless freedom is worth far more than a golden cage.
Memory Trigger: Freedom = Uncaged and free to fly!
Visual Icon: A bird soaring high out of an open cage door.

Definition: Unity or mutual support among individuals with a common purpose.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˌsɒl.ɪˈdær.ə.ti/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The wild parrot showed solidarity by giving a secret signal.
Memory Trigger: Solidarity = Standing united together!
Visual Icon: Two birds perching together side by side.

Definition: Outsmarted or defeated someone through superior cleverness.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˌaʊtˈwɪt.ɪd/ (Verb, Past Tense).
Textbook Context: The wise parrot outwitted the merchant and escaped.
Memory Trigger: Outwitted = Outsmarted by clever brains!
Visual Icon: A parrot wearing a tiny graduation cap flying away.

Definition: The quality of having experience, knowledge, and good judgment.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈwɪz.dəm/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: True wisdom helps overcome difficult captivity.
Memory Trigger: Wisdom = Smart thinking in tough times!
Visual Icon: An owl perched on a book glowing with light.

Definition: The condition of being imprisoned or confined against one's will.
Phonetic & Usage: /kæpˈtɪv.ə.ti/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: No bird can be happy living in lifelong captivity.
Memory Trigger: Captivity = Locked away from home!
Visual Icon: A padlock securing a cage door.

Definition: Rested or balanced on a branch, ledge, or high spot.
Phonetic & Usage: /pɜːtʃt/ (Verb, Past Tense).
Textbook Context: The bird perched on the window sill before flying away.
Memory Trigger: Perched = Sitting high on a perch!
Visual Icon: A parrot balanced gracefully on a tree branch.

Definition: Synonym for wise: Clever, sagacious, intelligent, or smart.
Phonetic & Usage: /waɪz/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The wise (clever) parrot devised a secret plan.
Memory Trigger: Wise and clever both mean sharp mind!
Visual Icon: An owl holding a scroll.

Definition: Antonym for freedom: Captivity, imprisonment, or bondage.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈfriː.dəm/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The bird chose freedom over captivity.
Memory Trigger: Freedom flies; Captivity locks up!
Visual Icon: An open cage next to a locked chain.

Definition: Synonym for feigned: Pretended, faked, or simulated.
Phonetic & Usage: /feɪnd/ (Verb).
Textbook Context: The bird feigned (pretended) to be dead.
Memory Trigger: Feigned and pretended mean fake action!
Visual Icon: A theater mask showing dual expressions.

Definition: Antonym for wealthy: Poor, needy, or impoverished.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈwɛl.θi/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The wealthy merchant bought a golden cage.
Memory Trigger: Wealthy has riches; Poor has little!
Visual Icon: A gold coin sack next to an empty coin pouch.

Definition: Antonym for sorrowfully: Joyfully, happily, or cheerfully.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈsɒr.oʊ.fəl.i/ (Adverb).
Textbook Context: He spoke sorrowfully, but the bird flew away joyfully.
Memory Trigger: Sorrowfully sheds tears; Joyfully smiles!
Visual Icon: A sad crying face next to a cheering happy face.

Definition: Antonym for beautiful: Ugly, plain, or hideous.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈbjuː.tɪ.fəl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The beautiful parrot had green feathers.
Memory Trigger: Beautiful is lovely to see!
Visual Icon: A glowing colorful feather next to a dull gray stone.

Definition: Antonym for alive: Dead, lifeless, or deceased.
Phonetic & Usage: /əˈlaɪv/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The parrot seemed dead, but was alive and clever.
Memory Trigger: Alive breathes; Dead stays still!
Visual Icon: A green growing sprout next to a dry fallen leaf.

Definition: Antonym for release: Imprison, capture, or detain.
Phonetic & Usage: /rɪˈliːs/ (Verb).
Textbook Context: He decided to release the bird from captivity.
Memory Trigger: Release sets free; Capture locks up!
Visual Icon: A hand opening to release a butterfly.

Definition: Antonym for wild: Tame, domesticated, or captive.
Phonetic & Usage: /waıld/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Wild birds love deep forests, while tame birds live in cages.
Memory Trigger: Wild lives in nature; Tame lives with humans!
Visual Icon: A forest wolf next to a pet puppy.

Definition: Antonym for heavy: Light, weightless, or feathery.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈhɛv.i/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The cage was heavy, but the parrot's wings were light.
Memory Trigger: Heavy presses down; Light floats up!
Visual Icon: A heavy iron weight next to a floating feather.

Definition: The letter 'g' is silent in 'feigned' (/feɪnd/), sign, reign, design.
Phonetic & Usage: /feɪnd/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The wild parrot feigned (/feɪnd/) death on the branch.
Memory Trigger: G stays silent in feigned!
Visual Icon: A parrot with a silent 'G' badge.

Definition: The letter 't' is silent before 'ch' in catch, match, watch, hatch.
Phonetic & Usage: /kætʃ/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The merchant could not catch the escaping bird.
Memory Trigger: T disappears before CH!
Visual Icon: A baseball glove catching a ball with silent 'T'.

Definition: The letter 'l' is silent before 'k' in talk, walk, chalk, folk.
Phonetic & Usage: /tɔːk/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The caged parrot learned to talk like humans.
Memory Trigger: L sleeps when you talk!
Visual Icon: A talking mouth icon with silent 'L'.

Definition: The digraph 'ch' makes a /tʃ/ sound in merchant, chair, chest.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈmɜː.tʃənt/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The merchant (/tʃ/) bought a golden cage.
Memory Trigger: CH says /tʃ/ like chin!
Visual Icon: A merchant hat with 'CH -> /tʃ/' tag.

Definition: The letter 'g' before 'e' in cage makes a soft /dʒ/ sound.
Phonetic & Usage: /keɪdʒ/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The parrot lived in a cage (/dʒ/).
Memory Trigger: G before E says soft /dʒ/!
Visual Icon: A cage icon with soft 'G' sound wave.

Definition: The letter 'w' is silent before 'h' in whole, who, whom, whose.
Phonetic & Usage: /hoʊl/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The whole forest cheered for the parrot's freedom.
Memory Trigger: W is silent in whole!
Visual Icon: A full circle with a ghosted 'W'.

Definition: The letter 'k' is silent before 'n' at the start of knowledge, knee, knife.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈnɒl.ɪdʒ/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Wisdom is practical knowledge put into action.
Memory Trigger: K is quiet in knowledge!
Visual Icon: An open book with silent 'K'.

Definition: The letter 'h' is silent after 'c' in echo, school, chorus, stomach.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɛk.oʊ/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Greetings echo through the forest trees.
Memory Trigger: H stays silent in echo!
Visual Icon: Sound waves bouncing off mountains.

Definition: Adverbs that describe HOW an action is performed (cleverly, sorrowfully, silently, swiftly).
Phonetic & Usage: Adverb Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: The parrot acted cleverly and flew away silently.
Memory Trigger: Adverbs of manner end in '-ly' and tell HOW!
Visual Icon: A running cat moving 'silently'.

Definition: Direct speech quotes exact words in quotation marks; Indirect speech reports speech without exact quotes.
Phonetic & Usage: Grammar Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: The bird said, 'Give my greetings.' / The bird asked him to give greetings.
Memory Trigger: Direct uses quotes; Indirect tells the story!
Visual Icon: Two speech bubbles - one with quotes, one plain.

Definition: Capitalizing specific names of wildlife reserves (Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary, Sultanpur).
Phonetic & Usage: Noun Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary protects thousands of migratory wild birds.
Memory Trigger: Specific sanctuary names need CAPITAL letters!
Visual Icon: A park sign reading 'Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary'.

Definition: Verbs expressing ability, possibility, or permission in past contexts (could fly, would escape).
Phonetic & Usage: Verb Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: The bird could fly high once freed from the cage.
Memory Trigger: Modals like COULD show ability in the past!
Visual Icon: A bird flexing wings with a 'CAN DO' badge.

Definition: Describing an ongoing action happening in past time (was flying, was perching).
Phonetic & Usage: Tense Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: The parrot was sitting on the branch when the merchant arrived.
Memory Trigger: Was/Were + -ING = Past Continuous!
Visual Icon: A timeline clock showing an ongoing past action.

Definition: Joining two related clauses using time conjunctions like 'when' or 'as soon as'.
Phonetic & Usage: Sentence Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: When the merchant opened the cage, the parrot flew away.
Memory Trigger: 'When' connects cause and time sequence!
Visual Icon: Two connected train cars labeled Clause 1 and Clause 2.

Definition: A special noun used to group animals together (a flock of wild parrots).
Phonetic & Usage: Noun Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: A flock of wild parrots lived in the green forest.
Memory Trigger: A FLOCK = A group of birds together!
Visual Icon: A sky illustration with a flock of 5 birds.

Definition: Adding the prefix 'un-' to a word to mean 'not' or opposite (un-happy, un-tamed).
Phonetic & Usage: Prefix Rule (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: A caged bird is unhappy and feels untamed longings.
Memory Trigger: UN- means NOT!
Visual Icon: A puzzle piece 'UN' attached to 'HAPPY'.

Definition: Wouldn't is the contraction for 'would not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈwʊd.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: The parrot wouldn't stay in captivity any longer.
Memory Trigger: Wouldn't = Would + Not!
Visual Icon: A bird refusing a cage door.

Definition: Shouldn't is the contraction for 'should not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈʃʊd.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: We shouldn't keep wild birds trapped in cages.
Memory Trigger: Shouldn't = Should + Not!
Visual Icon: A warning sign over a cage.

Definition: Haven't is the contraction for 'have not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈhæv.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: They haven't seen a bird as clever as this parrot.
Memory Trigger: Haven't = Have + Not!
Visual Icon: A blank bird perch.

Definition: You'll is the contraction for 'you will'.
Phonetic & Usage: /juːl/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: You'll find your wild friends in the forest.
Memory Trigger: You'll = You + Will!
Visual Icon: A finger pointing to a forest path.

Definition: She'd stands for 'she would' or 'she had'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ʃiːd/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: She'd escape the cage as soon as the door opened.
Memory Trigger: She'd = She + Would!
Visual Icon: A girl icon with a thought bubble.

Definition: That's is the contraction for 'that is'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ðæts/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: That's a very clever trick to gain freedom!
Memory Trigger: That's = That + Is!
Visual Icon: An approving thumbs-up icon.

Definition: Pretend to be motionless and dead to deceive an enemy or escape danger.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The wild parrot played dead on the forest branch.
Memory Trigger: Play dead = Lie still to fool others!
Visual Icon: A bird lying still on its back with eyes closed.

Definition: A luxurious or comfortable situation that nonetheless restricts one's freedom.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Even a golden cage is still a prison for a bird.
Memory Trigger: Golden cage = Luxury without liberty!
Visual Icon: A shiny gold cage adorned with jewels.

Definition: Extend one's capabilities, gain independence, and explore new opportunities.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The parrot opened the window to spread its wings.
Memory Trigger: Spread your wings = Fly free and explore!
Visual Icon: A bird opening wide wings soaring into sky.

Definition: Release someone or something from captivity or restraint.
Phonetic & Usage: Common Phrase (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The merchant unknowingly set the parrot free.
Memory Trigger: Set free = Open the lock and release!
Visual Icon: A hand unlatching a cage lock.

Definition: Something you already have is better than risking it for something uncertain.
Phonetic & Usage: Proverb / Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The merchant thought he had a bird in the hand.
Memory Trigger: A bird in hand = Valuing what you hold!
Visual Icon: A hand holding a small bird gently.

Definition: Appearing suddenly without warning from nowhere.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The parrot's escape plan seemed to come out of thin air.
Memory Trigger: Out of thin air = Magic trick appearance!
Visual Icon: A bird materializing from clouds.

flashcards.back_content:
Definition: A cold-blooded vertebrate animal that lives both in water and on land.
Phonetic & Usage: /æmˈfɪb.i.ən/ (Noun / Adjective).
Textbook Context: A frog is a cheerful amphibian that thrives in ponds and gardens.
Memory Trigger: Amphi = BOTH land and water life!
Visual Icon: A frog sitting on a lily pad next to a grassy riverbank.

Definition: The process of transformation from an immature form (tadpole) to an adult form.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˌmɛt.əˈmɔː.fə.sɪs/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: A swimming tadpole undergoes metamorphosis to become an adult frog.
Memory Trigger: Meta-morph-osis = Changing body shape!
Visual Icon: A diagram showing egg -> tadpole -> froglet -> adult frog.

Definition: The aquatic larva of a frog or toad, having a tail and gills.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈtæd.poʊl/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The tiny tadpole swims in the pond before growing legs.
Memory Trigger: Tadpole = Tail pole swimming in water!
Visual Icon: A small swimming tadpole with a long tail.

Definition: Having feet with skin connecting the toes, assisting in swimming.
Phonetic & Usage: /wɛbd/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Frogs have webbed feet that help them paddle swiftly in water.
Memory Trigger: Webbed feet act like swimming flippers!
Visual Icon: A close-up of a frog's webbed green foot.

Definition: Coated with an adhesive substance that catches insects.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈstɪk.i/ (Noun / Adjective).
Textbook Context: The frog uses its long sticky tongue to catch flying insects.
Memory Trigger: Sticky tongue snaps up flies instantly!
Visual Icon: A frog extending a long sticky pink tongue toward a fly.

Definition: Living on or relating to the land rather than in water or air.
Phonetic & Usage: /təˈrɛs.tri.əl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Adult frogs live a terrestrial life on land as well as in water.
Memory Trigger: Terrestrial = On Terra (land)!
Visual Icon: A frog hopping across green mossy ground.

Definition: Relating to or living in water.
Phonetic & Usage: /əˈkwæt.ɪk/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Tadpoles spend their early life in an aquatic environment.
Memory Trigger: Aquatic = In Aqua (water)!
Visual Icon: A blue pond with underwater plants.

Definition: Special physical characteristics that help an organism survive in its habitat.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˌæd.æpˈteɪ.ʃənz/ (Noun, Plural).
Textbook Context: Webbed feet and moist skin are key adaptations for frogs.
Memory Trigger: Adaptations help creatures survive!
Visual Icon: A frog showing webbed feet, large eyes, and moist skin.

Definition: The natural home or environment of an animal, plant, or organism.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈhæb.ɪ.tæt/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: A clean freshwater pond is the ideal habitat for frogs.
Memory Trigger: Habitat = Natural home!
Visual Icon: A lily pond surrounded by tall reeds.

Definition: A deep, hoarse sound made by a frog.
Phonetic & Usage: /kroʊk/ (Noun / Verb).
Textbook Context: In the evening, frogs croak loudly near the water.
Memory Trigger: Croak is the frog's signature sound!
Visual Icon: A frog puffing its vocal sac with sound waves.

Definition: Water or liquid diffused in small quantities as mist, vapor, or dew.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈmɔɪs.tʃər/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Frogs need skin moisture to breathe through their permeable skin.
Memory Trigger: Moisture keeps frog skin damp and healthy!
Visual Icon: Water droplets sparkling on a green frog back.

Definition: A small two-winged flying insect that frogs feed upon.
Phonetic & Usage: /næt/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The frog flicked its tongue to catch a tiny gnat.
Memory Trigger: Gnat = Tiny flying fly with silent G!
Visual Icon: A small winged insect flying near water.

Definition: Synonym for moist: Damp, humid, slick, or dewy.
Phonetic & Usage: /mɔɪst/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Frog skin remains moist (damp) all day.
Memory Trigger: Moist and damp describe soft wetness!
Visual Icon: Water drops on a green leaf.

Definition: Antonym for moist: Dry, arid, parched, or withered.
Phonetic & Usage: /mɔɪst/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Sunlight dries out frog skin, making it dry.
Memory Trigger: Moist is damp; Dry lacks liquid!
Visual Icon: A cracked dry mud puddle next to a clear lake.

Definition: Antonym for terrestrial: Aquatic, marine, or water-dwelling.
Phonetic & Usage: /təˈrɛs.tri.əl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Frogs switch between terrestrial and aquatic life.
Memory Trigger: Terrestrial = Land; Aquatic = Water!
Visual Icon: A split icon showing green grass and blue water.

Definition: Antonym for tiny: Huge, gigantic, immense, or massive.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈtaɪ.ni/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Tadpoles are tiny, but adult bullfrogs are huge.
Memory Trigger: Tiny is small; Huge is massive!
Visual Icon: A tiny tadpole beside a large frog.

Definition: Synonym for swift: Fast, rapid, nimble, or brisk.
Phonetic & Usage: /swɪft/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Webbed feet make the frog a swift (fast) swimmer.
Memory Trigger: Swift and rapid mean high speed!
Visual Icon: A frog zooming underwater with speed trails.

Definition: Antonym for hidden: Visible, exposed, or obvious.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈhɪd.ən/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The frog stayed hidden under the lily pad.
Memory Trigger: Hidden conceals; Visible exposes!
Visual Icon: A frog peeking out from under a leaf.

Definition: Antonym for soft: Hard, rigid, or tough.
Phonetic & Usage: /sɒft/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Frog skin is soft, but turtle shells are hard.
Memory Trigger: Soft yields to touch; Hard stays firm!
Visual Icon: A soft sponge next to a hard stone.

Definition: Antonym for clean: Polluted, dirty, or muddy.
Phonetic & Usage: /kliːn/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Frogs need clean pond water rather than polluted streams.
Memory Trigger: Clean is pure; Polluted is dirty!
Visual Icon: A clear water drop next to a dark muddy drop.

Definition: Antonym for healthy: Sick, diseased, or frail.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈhɛl.θi/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: A clean habitat keeps frogs healthy.
Memory Trigger: Healthy thrives; Sick suffers!
Visual Icon: A vibrant green frog hopping happily.

Definition: Antonym for smooth: Bumpy, rough, or warty.
Phonetic & Usage: /smuːð/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Frogs have smooth skin, while toads have bumpy skin.
Memory Trigger: Smooth is sleek; Bumpy has warts!
Visual Icon: A sleek frog next to a rough warty toad.

Definition: The letter 'g' is silent when followed by 'n' in gnat, gnaw, gnu.
Phonetic & Usage: /næt/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The frog snapped up a tiny gnat (/næt/).
Memory Trigger: G stays quiet in gnat!
Visual Icon: A tiny fly with a silent 'G' crossed out.

Definition: The letter 't' is silent in listen, glisten, fasten, castle.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈlɪs.ən/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Listen (/lɪs.ən/) to the frogs croaking at night.
Memory Trigger: T stays silent in listen!
Visual Icon: An ear icon with a muted letter 'T'.

Definition: The short vowel 'o' makes an /ɒ/ sound in frog, pond, log, spot.
Phonetic & Usage: /frɒɡ/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The green frog (/frɒɡ/) sat on the log.
Memory Trigger: Short O says /ɒ/ like hop!
Visual Icon: A frog hopping over 'F-R-O-G'.

Definition: Hard 'g' in frog (/ɡ/) vs hard 'p' blend in tadpole.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈtæd.poʊl/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: A tadpole swims using its tail.
Memory Trigger: Tadpole has two distinct syllables!
Visual Icon: A tadpole diagram split into TAD - POLE.

Definition: The vowel pair 'oi' makes an /ɔɪ/ sound in moist, point, coin, join.
Phonetic & Usage: /mɔɪst/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Frog skin must remain moist (/mɔɪst/).
Memory Trigger: OI says /ɔɪ/ like coin!
Visual Icon: Water droplets with 'OI' highlighted.

Definition: The letter 'b' is silent after 'm' in thumb, limb, climb, comb.
Phonetic & Usage: /θʌm/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The frog is as small as a human thumb.
Memory Trigger: B is quiet after M in thumb!
Visual Icon: A hand thumbs-up with silent 'B'.

Definition: The letter 'p' is silent before 's' in psalm, psychology.
Phonetic & Usage: /sɑːm/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The frogs sang a nocturnal pond psalm.
Memory Trigger: P sleeps before S!
Visual Icon: A musical note with a muted 'P'.

Definition: The letter 'k' is silent before 'n' in knee, kneel, knot.
Phonetic & Usage: /niː/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The frog bent its back legs at the knee.
Memory Trigger: K is silent before N!
Visual Icon: A frog hind leg joint with silent 'K'.

Definition: Forming present continuous verbs using is/are + verb-ing (is swimming, are croaking).
Phonetic & Usage: Tense Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: The frog is leaping on the leaf; tadpoles are swimming.
Memory Trigger: IS/ARE + VERB-ING shows action happening NOW!
Visual Icon: A frog mid-leap with 'LEAPING' action text.

Definition: Combining two nouns to form a single new word (pond + weed = pondweed).
Phonetic & Usage: Word Formation (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Dragonflies and pondweed populate the lily pond.
Memory Trigger: Combine two words to create one!
Visual Icon: Icons of Dragon + Fly = Dragonfly.

Definition: Words that imitate the natural sound associated with an action or animal.
Phonetic & Usage: Literary Device (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Croak! Splash! The frog hit the water with a plop!
Memory Trigger: Onomatopoeia words SOUND like what they do!
Visual Icon: Sound effect bursts: 'CROAK!', 'PLOP!', 'SPLASH!'

Definition: Words like 'because' and 'so that' that connect a cause to its result.
Phonetic & Usage: Conjunction Rule (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Frogs have webbed feet SO THAT they can swim fast.
Memory Trigger: 'Because' gives the reason; 'So that' gives the purpose!
Visual Icon: Two puzzle pieces: Cause -> Effect.

Definition: Prepositions describing living spaces (in water, on land, under lily pads).
Phonetic & Usage: Preposition Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Frogs live ON land and IN freshwater ponds.
Memory Trigger: Prepositions place animals in their habitat!
Visual Icon: A frog ON a pad, IN water, UNDER a leaf.

Definition: Singular subjects take singular verbs (frog leaps); plural subjects take plural verbs (frogs leap).
Phonetic & Usage: Grammar Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: One frog croaks; three frogs croak together.
Memory Trigger: Singular adds -S; Plural drops -S!
Visual Icon: 1 frog -> croaks; 3 frogs -> croak.

Definition: Adjectives describing physical traits (green, sticky, webbed, moist).
Phonetic & Usage: Adjective Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: The green frog extended its long sticky tongue.
Memory Trigger: Adjectives paint pictures of nouns!
Visual Icon: A green frog with descriptive labels.

Definition: General knowledge link in EVS: The Ganges River Dolphin is India's National Aquatic Animal.
Phonetic & Usage: EVS Integration (General Knowledge).
Textbook Context: The Ganges River Dolphin shares clean freshwater habitats.
Memory Trigger: Protect clean freshwater for all aquatic life!
Visual Icon: A river dolphin jumping gracefully in a river.

Definition: It's is the contraction for 'it is' or 'it has'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ɪts/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: It's an amphibious creature living in the pond.
Memory Trigger: It's = It + Is!
Visual Icon: A frog pointing to itself.

Definition: They're is the contraction for 'they are'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ðɛər/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: They're swimming as tadpoles before growing legs.
Memory Trigger: They're = They + Are!
Visual Icon: A swarm of tadpoles.

Definition: Can't is the contraction for 'cannot'.
Phonetic & Usage: /kɑːnt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: Tadpoles can't live on dry land without lungs.
Memory Trigger: Can't = Can + Not!
Visual Icon: A tadpole underwater.

Definition: Aren't is the contraction for 'are not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ɑːnt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: Frogs aren't reptiles; they are amphibians.
Memory Trigger: Aren't = Are + Not!
Visual Icon: A frog next to a lizard with an X.

Definition: Doesn't is the contraction for 'does not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈdʌz.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: A tadpole doesn't have lungs in early life.
Memory Trigger: Doesn't = Does + Not!
Visual Icon: A small tadpole with gills.

Definition: I'm is the contraction for 'I am'.
Phonetic & Usage: /aɪm/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: I'm a cheerful frog leaping on the green pad!
Memory Trigger: I'm = I + Am!
Visual Icon: A smiling frog wearing a name tag.

flashcards.back_content:
Definition: An important or prominent person in a small, restricted group.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The bullfrog felt like a big fish in a small pond.
Memory Trigger: Big fish = Important in a small circle!
Visual Icon: A huge frog occupying most of a tiny lily puddle.

flashcards.front_content: Like a fish out of water
flashcards.back_content:
Definition: Feeling uncomfortable, awkward, or out of place in an unfamiliar setting.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Without moisture, a frog feels like a fish out of water.
Memory Trigger: Fish out of water = Uncomfortable and helpless!
Visual Icon: A fish stranded on dry sand looking for water.

Definition: An act of believing or trying something uncertain with confidence.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The frog took a leap of faith across the wide stream.
Memory Trigger: Leap of faith = Jumping forward with trust!
Visual Icon: A frog leaping across a gap between two river rocks.

Definition: Inexperienced, young, or immature.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The newly metamorphosed froglet was still wet behind the ears.
Memory Trigger: Wet behind ears = Young and inexperienced!
Visual Icon: A tiny froglet freshly emerged from a tadpole state.

Definition: The habitat and life cycle encompassing both land and aquatic domains.
Phonetic & Usage: /æmˈfɪb.i.ən/ (Common Phrase).
Textbook Context: Welcome to the frog's fascinating amphibian world!
Memory Trigger: Two domains in one life!
Visual Icon: A frog resting on a lily pad bridging land and water.

Definition: Existing or operating in two distinct environments or roles.
Phonetic & Usage: Common Phrase (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Frogs lead a dual life on land and in freshwater.
Memory Trigger: Dual life = Double habitat existence!
Visual Icon: A split icon showing land and water.
