flashcards.back_content:
Definition: A large natural or artificial lake used as a source of water supply.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈrɛz.ə.vwɑːr/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Rooftop water tanks act as personal domestic reservoirs.
Memory Trigger: Reservoir = Reserve water for later!
Visual Icon: A large rooftop water tank with pipes.

Definition: The preservation and careful management of natural resources like water.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˌkɒn.səˈveɪ.ʃən/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Water conservation helps communities survive hot summer droughts.
Memory Trigger: Conserve water to preserve life!
Visual Icon: A green leaf cradling a clean blue water drop.

Definition: Water that falls as rain and can be collected for domestic use.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈreɪn.wɔː.tər/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Rainwater harvesting collects clean rain from rooftops into tanks.
Memory Trigger: Rain + Water = Free clean water!
Visual Icon: Raindrops falling into a collection funnel and tank.

Definition: Collecting and storing a natural resource (like rainwater) for future use.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈhɑː.vɪ.stɪŋ/ (Noun / Verb).
Textbook Context: Rainwater harvesting prevents water scarcity during dry summers.
Memory Trigger: Harvest rain like harvesting crops!
Visual Icon: A rooftop pipeline feeding a large storage tank.

Definition: A person who designs buildings and storage structures.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɑː.kɪ.tɛkt/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Innovative builders in Punjab design tractor-shaped water tanks.
Memory Trigger: Architects design smart structures!
Visual Icon: An architect holding blueprints next to a building.

Definition: A prolonged period of abnormally low rainfall, leading to a water shortage.
Phonetic & Usage: /draʊt/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Sumat experienced severe tap water shortages during the summer drought.
Memory Trigger: Drought = Dry out without rain!
Visual Icon: Cracked dry soil under a blazing sun.

Definition: Relating to the running of a home or family household.
Phonetic & Usage: /dəˈmɛs.tɪk/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Custom tanks supply water for daily domestic chores like washing.
Memory Trigger: Domestic = Home and family!
Visual Icon: A house icon showing kitchen and bathroom taps.

Definition: The state of being scarce or in short supply; shortage.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈskɛər.sə.ti/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Water scarcity teaches us the true value of every single drop.
Memory Trigger: Scarcity = Shortage of supplies!
Visual Icon: An empty water jug with one last drop falling.

Definition: The action or method of keeping or storing items for future use.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈstɔː.rɪdʒ/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Underground Tankas in Rajasthan provide year-round water storage.
Memory Trigger: Storage keeps water safe until needed!
Visual Icon: An underground concrete storage tank.

Definition: Able to be maintained at a certain rate without depleting resources.
Phonetic & Usage: /səˈsteɪ.nə.bəl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Harvesting rainwater is a sustainable solution to dry climates.
Memory Trigger: Sustainable = Lasts for future generations!
Visual Icon: An infinity symbol made of green leaves and water drops.

Definition: Made or modified to order for a particular customer.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈkʌs.təm/ (Adjective / Noun).
Textbook Context: Punjabi homeowners build custom water tanks shaped like tractors.
Memory Trigger: Custom = Uniquely made for you!
Visual Icon: A water tank sculpted in the shape of a red tractor.

Definition: A powerful motor vehicle used on farms, often sculpted as a tank shape.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈtræk.tər/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: A rooftop water tank sculpted like a tractor overlooks the village field.
Memory Trigger: Tractors power farms and inspire tank designs!
Visual Icon: A red farm tractor perched atop a house roof.

Definition: Synonym for save: Preserve, conserve, store, or protect.
Phonetic & Usage: /seɪv/ (Verb).
Textbook Context: Save (conserve) every drop of water.
Memory Trigger: Save and conserve both mean protect from waste!
Visual Icon: A hand protecting a water drop.

Definition: Antonym for save: Waste, squander, or deplete.
Phonetic & Usage: /seɪv/ (Verb).
Textbook Context: Do not waste water; save it!
Memory Trigger: Save keeps; Waste throws away!
Visual Icon: A running tap overflowing into a drain.

Definition: Antonym for scarcity: Abundance, plenty, or surplus.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈskɛər.sə.ti/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Rain harvesting turns water scarcity into abundance.
Memory Trigger: Scarcity is shortage; Abundance is plenty!
Visual Icon: An empty bucket next to an overflowing tub.

Definition: Antonym for clean: Contaminated, dirty, or polluted.
Phonetic & Usage: /kliːn/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Store clean rainwater in sealed tanks to prevent contamination.
Memory Trigger: Clean is pure; Contaminated is unsafe!
Visual Icon: A clear water glass next to a murky glass.

Definition: Antonym for dry: Wet, moist, or soaked.
Phonetic & Usage: /draɪ/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Dry summer days require wet water storage.
Memory Trigger: Dry lacks water; Wet holds water!
Visual Icon: A desert sun icon next to a rain cloud icon.

Definition: Antonym for custom: Standard, ordinary, or generic.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈkʌs.təm/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Instead of a generic cylinder, they built a custom tractor tank.
Memory Trigger: Custom is unique; Generic is plain!
Visual Icon: A unique tractor tank next to a plain cylinder.

Definition: Antonym for full: Empty, drained, or vacant.
Phonetic & Usage: /fʊl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The tank was full after rain, but empty during drought.
Memory Trigger: Full overflows; Empty has nothing!
Visual Icon: A full glass of water next to an empty glass.

Definition: Antonym for useful: Useless, ineffective, or futile.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈjuːs.fəl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Custom tanks are attractive and very useful.
Memory Trigger: Useful helps; Useless fails!
Visual Icon: A working water tap icon.

Definition: Antonym for heavy: Light, slight, or gentle.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈhɛv.i/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Heavy monsoon rain fills underground storage tanks.
Memory Trigger: Heavy is dense; Light is small!
Visual Icon: A heavy rain cloud with many raindrops.

Definition: Synonym for community: Society, neighborhood, or collective.
Phonetic & Usage: /kəˈmjuː.nə.ti/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The whole community (neighborhood) joined the water drive.
Memory Trigger: Community = People working together!
Visual Icon: A group of village houses joined by hands.

Definition: The letter 'h' is silent after 'w' in whack, what, where, when, why.
Phonetic & Usage: /wæk/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: What (/wɒt/) a tank! Water hit the bucket with a whack.
Memory Trigger: H is silent after W!
Visual Icon: A question mark over a silent 'H'.

Definition: The letter 'l' is silent in should, would, could, half, talk.
Phonetic & Usage: /ʃʊd/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: We should (/ʃʊd/) conserve every drop of water.
Memory Trigger: L stays quiet in should!
Visual Icon: A thumbs-up icon with a muted 'L'.

Definition: The letter 'c' before 'u', 'a', 'o' makes a hard /k/ sound.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈkʌs.təm/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: They built a custom (/k/) rooftop tank.
Memory Trigger: C before U says hard /k/!
Visual Icon: A wrench icon with hard 'C' sound wave.

Definition: The vowel pair 'ou' in drought makes an /aʊ/ sound, while '-gh-' is silent.
Phonetic & Usage: /draʊt/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The dry summer drought (/draʊt/) caused water shortages.
Memory Trigger: OU says /aʊ/; GH is silent!
Visual Icon: Cracked soil with silent 'GH' crossed out.

Definition: The letter 'c' before 'i' or 'e' makes a soft /s/ sound as in city, scarcity.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈsɪt.i/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Water scarcity (/s/) affected the whole city.
Memory Trigger: C before I says soft /s/!
Visual Icon: A city skyline with an 'S' sound wave.

Definition: The letter 't' is silent in castle, listen, rustle, whistle.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈkɑː.səl/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The rooftop tank looked like a miniature castle.
Memory Trigger: T sleeps in castle!
Visual Icon: A castle tower with a muted 'T'.

Definition: The letter 'w' is silent in answer, sword, two, write.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɑːn.sər/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Rainwater harvesting is the answer to drought.
Memory Trigger: W is silent in answer!
Visual Icon: A speech bubble with a green checkmark.

Definition: The letter 'k' is silent before 'n' in know, knowledge, knot.
Phonetic & Usage: /neʊ/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: We know that water is essential for life.
Memory Trigger: K is silent before N!
Visual Icon: An open book with silent 'K'.

Definition: Verbs that express necessity, duty, or advice (must, should, ought to, need to).
Phonetic & Usage: Grammar Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: We MUST save water; everyone SHOULD close running taps.
Memory Trigger: MUST = Obligation; SHOULD = Good advice!
Visual Icon: A green shield with 'MUST SAVE WATER' text.

Definition: Command sentences starting with a verb used to give instructions or slogans.
Phonetic & Usage: Sentence Type (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Save every drop! Turn off running taps! Harvest rainwater!
Memory Trigger: Imperatives give clear direct commands!
Visual Icon: A megaphone icon broadcasting slogans.

Definition: Nouns formed by combining two distinct words (rain + water, roof + top).
Phonetic & Usage: Word Formation (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Rainwater flows off the rooftop into the pipeline.
Memory Trigger: Two words join to make one compound noun!
Visual Icon: Roof + Top = Rooftop.

Definition: Expressing future intentions using 'will' or 'shall' (will install, shall harvest).
Phonetic & Usage: Tense Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Our village will install rainwater tanks next summer.
Memory Trigger: WILL + VERB describes future plans!
Visual Icon: A calendar pointing to next month.

Definition: Prepositions showing source or containment (from rooftops, inside tanks, out of taps).
Phonetic & Usage: Preposition Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Water flows FROM rooftops INSIDE underground Tankas.
Memory Trigger: Prepositions map origin and destination!
Visual Icon: An arrow flowing FROM a roof INTO a tank.

Definition: Describing processes where the action is emphasized over the performer.
Phonetic & Usage: Grammar Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Rainwater is collected and stored in underground tanks.
Memory Trigger: Passive Voice: Object + IS/ARE + Past Participle!
Visual Icon: A factory pipeline diagram showing process steps.

Definition: Expressing awe or admiration using 'What a...' or 'How...!'
Phonetic & Usage: Sentence Type (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: What a tank! What a clever rainwater design!
Memory Trigger: Exclamations express wonder and awe!
Visual Icon: A starburst speech bubble reading 'What a tank!'

Definition: Determiners expressing total amount or individual items in a group.
Phonetic & Usage: Adjective Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Every drop counts; all households should participate.
Memory Trigger: Every = Each individual one; All = Entire total!
Visual Icon: A collection of individual drops forming a full bucket.

Definition: Shouldn't is the contraction for 'should not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈʃʊd.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: We shouldn't let tap water run wastefully.
Memory Trigger: Shouldn't = Should + Not!
Visual Icon: A tap with a red X.

Definition: Mustn't is the contraction for 'must not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈmʌs.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: You mustn't pollute clean drinking water storage.
Memory Trigger: Mustn't = Must + Not!
Visual Icon: A warning sign over a reservoir.

Definition: We'll is the contraction for 'we will'.
Phonetic & Usage: /wiːl/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: We'll build a rooftop rainwater tank together.
Memory Trigger: We'll = We + Will!
Visual Icon: A team holding construction blueprints.

Definition: Don't is the contraction for 'do not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /doʊnt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: Don't waste water during the summer heat.
Memory Trigger: Don't = Do + Not!
Visual Icon: A hand stop gesture icon.

Definition: There'll is the contraction for 'there will'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ðɛər.əl/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: There'll be plenty of water if we harvest rain.
Memory Trigger: There'll = There + Will!
Visual Icon: A full water tank icon.

Definition: Couldn't is the contraction for 'could not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈkʊd.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: Suma couldn't get tap water during the drought.
Memory Trigger: Couldn't = Could + Not!
Visual Icon: An empty water tap.

Definition: Conserve all available water without wasting any small amount.
Phonetic & Usage: Conservation Slogan (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Our school campaign encourages everyone to save every drop.
Memory Trigger: Save every drop = Every drop is precious!
Visual Icon: A single water droplet cradled in hands.

Definition: A tiny, insignificant amount compared to what is needed.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: One small tank is just a drop in the ocean, but many tanks help.
Memory Trigger: A drop in the ocean = Small part of a huge whole!
Visual Icon: One small drop falling into a vast ocean.

Definition: Reserve money or resources for a future time of need or hardship.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Collecting water is literally saving for a rainy day!
Memory Trigger: Save for a rainy day = Prepare for future need!
Visual Icon: A piggy bank holding a water drop icon.

Definition: Close a water faucet to prevent waste.
Phonetic & Usage: Action Phrase (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Always turn off the tap while brushing your teeth.
Memory Trigger: Turn off the tap = Stop running water!
Visual Icon: A hand turning a faucet knob off.

Definition: A fundamental truth emphasizing that water sustains all living organisms.
Phonetic & Usage: Motto / Slogan (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Remember that water is life; conserve it daily!
Memory Trigger: Water is life = Essential for all living things!
Visual Icon: A water drop with a green plant growing inside.

Definition: In serious trouble or facing a difficult crisis.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Without water storage, the village was in deep water during summer.
Memory Trigger: In deep water = Facing big trouble!
Visual Icon: A figure wading through deep water waves.

flashcards.back_content:
Definition: A small wooden peg tapered at both ends used in traditional Gilli Danda.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɡɪl.i/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The player flicked the small wooden gilli into the air.
Memory Trigger: Gilli = Small wooden peg with pointed tips!
Visual Icon: A small wooden peg tapered sharp at both ends.

Definition: A longer wooden stick used as a bat to strike the gilli.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈdʌn.dɑː/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: He struck the gilli forcefully using his wooden danda.
Memory Trigger: Danda = Long striking wooden stick!
Visual Icon: A smooth wooden stick held like a bat.

Definition: Diminished or narrowed gradually toward one end.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈteɪ.pəd/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The gilli is tapered at both tips to bounce off the ground when hit.
Memory Trigger: Tapered = Narrowing to a point!
Visual Icon: A wooden cylinder narrowing to sharp ends.

Definition: Hitting or delivering a blow with a stick or bat.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈstraɪ.kɪŋ/ (Verb / Adjective).
Textbook Context: Striking the gilli requires keen hand-eye coordination.
Memory Trigger: Striking = Hitting with power!
Visual Icon: A danda hitting a gilli mid-air with motion sparks.

Definition: Fair, generous, and polite behavior during a game.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈspɔːts.mən.ʃɪp/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Playing Gilli Danda fosters camaraderie and sportsmanship.
Memory Trigger: Sportsmanship = Play fair and respect all!
Visual Icon: Two players giving a high-five after a game.

Definition: Mutual trust, friendship, and goodwill among companions.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˌkæm.əˈrɑː.dər.i/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Traditional street games create deep camaraderie among village youth.
Memory Trigger: Camaraderie = Close friendship among teammates!
Visual Icon: A group of children sitting together laughing after play.

Definition: Originating or occurring naturally in a particular region; native.
Phonetic & Usage: /ɪnˈdɪdʒ.ɪ.nəs/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Gilli Danda is an indigenous Indian outdoor sport.
Memory Trigger: Indigenous = Native traditional craft or game!
Visual Icon: A map of India decorated with traditional sports gear.

Definition: In accordance with longstanding custom or heritage.
Phonetic & Usage: /trəˈdɪʃ.ən.əl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Gilli Danda requires no expensive gear—only traditional wooden pieces.
Memory Trigger: Traditional = Passed down through customs!
Visual Icon: Handcrafted wooden play gear lying on grass.

Definition: The necessary items for a particular purpose or game.
Phonetic & Usage: /ɪˈkwɪp.mənt/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Children craft their own equipment using fallen tree branches.
Memory Trigger: Equipment = Tools needed for play!
Visual Icon: A wooden danda and gilli set.

Definition: Strike forcefully with a sharp blow.
Phonetic & Usage: /wæk/ (Verb / Onomatopoeia).
Textbook Context: Whack! The danda launched the gilli high across the field.
Memory Trigger: Whack is the sharp sound of a hard hit!
Visual Icon: A sound effect burst reading 'WHACK!'.

Definition: An even distribution of weight enabling someone to remain upright.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈbæl.əns/ (Noun / Verb).
Textbook Context: The player maintained his balance while flicking the gilli.
Memory Trigger: Balance keeps you steady on your feet!
Visual Icon: A figure standing balanced on one leg.

Definition: The number of points or runs gained in a game.
Phonetic & Usage: /skɔːr/ (Noun / Verb).
Textbook Context: They measured distances with the danda to calculate the score.
Memory Trigger: Score = Total points earned!
Visual Icon: A wooden tally board with chalk points.

Definition: Synonym for traditional: Customary, native, heritage, or ancestral.
Phonetic & Usage: /trəˈdɪʃ.ən.əl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Gilli Danda is a traditional (customary) Indian game.
Memory Trigger: Traditional and customary mean ancestral ways!
Visual Icon: Ancient wooden play pieces.

Definition: Antonym for traditional: Modern, contemporary, or novel.
Phonetic & Usage: /trəˈdɪʃ.ən.əl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Traditional street games contrast with modern video games.
Memory Trigger: Traditional is ancestral; Modern is brand new!
Visual Icon: A wooden stick next to a modern gaming controller.

Definition: Synonym for sportsmanship: Fair play, honor, or integrity.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈspɔːts.mən.ʃɪp/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The team won praise for fair play (sportsmanship).
Memory Trigger: Sportsmanship and fair play mean playing by rules!
Visual Icon: A golden handshake trophy.

Definition: Antonym for tapered: Broadened, widened, or blunt.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈteɪ.pəd/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The gilli is tapered at tips, but the danda is blunt.
Memory Trigger: Tapered narrows; Blunt stays wide!
Visual Icon: A pointed peg next to a flat block.

Definition: Antonym for sharp: Dull, blunt, or rounded.
Phonetic & Usage: /ʃɑːp/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Keep the gilli tips tapered but not dangerously sharp.
Memory Trigger: Sharp cuts; Blunt is rounded!
Visual Icon: A sharp point next to a rounded edge.

Definition: Antonym for victorious: Defeated, vanquished, or losing.
Phonetic & Usage: /vɪkˈtɔː.ri.əs/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The victorious player cheered politely for the losing side.
Memory Trigger: Victorious wins; Defeated loses!
Visual Icon: A winner standing on a pedestal.

Definition: Antonym for rough: Smooth, polished, or slick.
Phonetic & Usage: /rʌf/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: They carved the rough branch until it was smooth.
Memory Trigger: Rough has bumps; Smooth feels slick!
Visual Icon: Unpolished wood next to smooth polished wood.

Definition: Synonym for rapid: Swift, quick, brisk, or fast.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈræp.ɪd/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The gilli flew with rapid (swift) speed.
Memory Trigger: Rapid and swift mean high velocity!
Visual Icon: A streak of light moving fast.

Definition: Antonym for skillful: Clumsy, awkward, or inexpert.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈskɪl.fəl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Practice turns a clumsy hitter into a skillful player.
Memory Trigger: Skillful is expert; Clumsy stumbles!
Visual Icon: An acrobat balancing gracefully.

Definition: Antonym for simple: Complex, elaborate, or complicated.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈsɪm.pəl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Gilli Danda has simple rules compared to complex cricket.
Memory Trigger: Simple is easy; Complex has many parts!
Visual Icon: A basic wooden peg next to a complex machine.

Definition: The letter 'h' is silent after 'w' in whack, whip, wheel, white.
Phonetic & Usage: /wæk/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Whack! (/wæk/) The danda hit the gilli.
Memory Trigger: H stays silent after W!
Visual Icon: A whip with silent 'H' crossed out.

Definition: The letter 'k' is silent before 'n' in knock, knee, knife.
Phonetic & Usage: /nɒk/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: He gave the gilli a clever knock.
Memory Trigger: K sleeps before N!
Visual Icon: A hand knocking on wood with silent 'K'.

Definition: The double consonant 'll' makes a short clear /l/ sound in gilli, ball, call.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɡɪl.i/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Gilli (/ˈɡɪl.i/) is carved from hardwood.
Memory Trigger: Double L makes one clean /l/ sound!
Visual Icon: Two letters 'L' merged into one sound block.

Definition: The vowel 'a' in danda makes a short broad /ʌ/ sound (/dʌn.dɑː/).
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈdʌn.dɑː/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Hold the danda (/dʌn.dɑː/) firmly in your hands.
Memory Trigger: Danda uses broad short /ʌ/ sounds!
Visual Icon: A danda stick labeled with phonetic guide.

Definition: The letter 'w' is silent before 'r' in wrist, write, wrong.
Phonetic & Usage: /rɪst/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Flick your wrist to launch the gilli.
Memory Trigger: W rests before R!
Visual Icon: A wrist joint with ghosted silent 'W'.

Definition: The letter 'g' is silent in design, sign, reign.
Phonetic & Usage: /dɪˈzaɪn/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Children design their own homemade wooden gear.
Memory Trigger: G is silent in design!
Visual Icon: A blueprint paper with muted 'G'.

Definition: The letter 'b' is silent after 'm' at the end of limb, climb, comb.
Phonetic & Usage: /lɪm/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: They cut fallen limbs from tree trunks.
Memory Trigger: B is quiet after M in limb!
Visual Icon: A tree branch with silent 'B'.

Definition: Long 'i' in strike (/straɪk/) vs short 'i' in gilli (/ɡɪl.i/).
Phonetic & Usage: /straɪk/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Strike the gilli sharply with the danda.
Memory Trigger: Strike has long 'i'; Gilli has short 'i'!
Visual Icon: A phonetic contrast chart: Strike vs Gilli.

Definition: Nouns representing intangible concepts, feelings, or qualities (sportsmanship, courage, friendship, skill).
Phonetic & Usage: Noun Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Sportsmanship and friendship are abstract nouns.
Memory Trigger: Abstract nouns can't be touched, but they exist in our hearts!
Visual Icon: A heart and brain icon connected by light.

Definition: Pronouns showing ownership without repeating nouns (mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs).
Phonetic & Usage: Pronoun Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: This danda is mine; that gilli is yours.
Memory Trigger: Possessive pronouns replace 'my stick' with 'mine'!
Visual Icon: Hands holding gear labeled MINE and YOURS.

Definition: Dynamic verbs describing forceful movement (struck, flicked, launched, caught).
Phonetic & Usage: Verb Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: He struck the gilli and launched it into the sky.
Memory Trigger: Action verbs bring sports stories to life!
Visual Icon: A stick hitting a peg with speed streaks.

Definition: Direct command sentences stating game guidelines.
Phonetic & Usage: Sentence Type (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Keep your eyes on the gilli! Measure the distance clearly!
Memory Trigger: Commands tell players what to do!
Visual Icon: A rulebook with bullet points.

Definition: Using simple past tense verbs to recount game events (carved, struck, measured, won).
Phonetic & Usage: Tense Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Gopi carved a danda and struck the gilli across the lawn.
Memory Trigger: Past Simple recounts completed story events!
Visual Icon: A storybook page showing past events.

Definition: Comparing two game items using '-er' (the danda is longer than the gilli).
Phonetic & Usage: Adjective Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: The danda is longer; the gilli is sharper.
Memory Trigger: Add -ER to compare two objects!
Visual Icon: A long stick next to a shorter peg with -ER label.

Definition: Adding '-s' or '-es' to indicate multiple people or items (player -> players).
Phonetic & Usage: Noun Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: All the players followed the traditional rules.
Memory Trigger: Plurals mean more than one!
Visual Icon: Icons of 1 player vs 4 players.

Definition: Question sentences used to count scores or decide turns (How many danda lengths? Who is next?).
Phonetic & Usage: Sentence Type (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: How many danda lengths did the gilli fly?
Memory Trigger: Interrogatives ask questions to score points!
Visual Icon: A question mark over a score card.

Definition: Let's is the contraction for 'let us'.
Phonetic & Usage: /lɛts/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: Let's play a round of Gilli Danda after school!
Memory Trigger: Let's = Let + Us!
Visual Icon: Children holding hands in a circle.

Definition: We're is the contraction for 'we are'.
Phonetic & Usage: /wɪər/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: We're crafting our own danda sticks from branches.
Memory Trigger: We're = We + Are!
Visual Icon: Two players carving wood.

Definition: It's is the contraction for 'it is'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ɪts/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: It's an ancient traditional Indian sport.
Memory Trigger: It's = It + Is!
Visual Icon: A finger pointing to a game set.

Definition: Who's is the contraction for 'who is'.
Phonetic & Usage: /huːz/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: Who's ready to strike the gilli next?
Memory Trigger: Who's = Who + Is!
Visual Icon: A player stepping up to bat.

Definition: You're is the contraction for 'you are'.
Phonetic & Usage: /jʊər/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: You're a very skillful hitter!
Memory Trigger: You're = You + Are!
Visual Icon: A cheering friend giving thumbs up.

Definition: They'll is the contraction for 'they will'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ðeɪl/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: They'll measure the winning distance with the danda.
Memory Trigger: They'll = They + Will!
Visual Icon: A team measuring ground distance.

Definition: Respect for rules, equal treatment, and sportsmanship in a game.
Phonetic & Usage: Common Phrase (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Gilli Danda teaches fair play and honest scoring.
Memory Trigger: Fair play = Honor and truth in sports!
Visual Icon: A scale balanced with a ball and heart.

Definition: Achieve a goal or hit a target successfully.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The player struck the gilli and hit the mark.
Memory Trigger: Hit the mark = Bullseye success!
Visual Icon: An arrow hitting a bullseye target.

Definition: Deliver a decisive hit or action in a match.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: He struck a decisive blow with his sturdy danda.
Memory Trigger: Strike a blow = Strong impact!
Visual Icon: A lightning spark off a wooden stick.

Definition: A situation where everyone has an equal opportunity to succeed.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Traditional games offer a level playing field for all village kids.
Memory Trigger: Level playing field = Equal chances for all!
Visual Icon: A flat green field icon.

Definition: Outside the designated play area boundary.
Phonetic & Usage: Sports Phrase (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The gilli landed out of bounds behind the garden fence.
Memory Trigger: Out of bounds = Outside the play zone!
Visual Icon: A red X outside a fence boundary.

Definition: Feelings of camaraderie, loyalty, and enthusiasm among team members.
Phonetic & Usage: Common Phrase (Phrase).
Textbook Context: High fives and cheers showed their wonderful team spirit.
Memory Trigger: Team spirit = Supporting your teammates!
Visual Icon: Hands joined in a central circle.

flashcards.back_content:
Definition: A traditional village council of elders in India responsible for governance and resolving disputes.
Phonetic & Usage: /pʌnˈtʃɑː.jət/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The Panchayat assembled under the banyan tree to resolve the dispute.
Memory Trigger: Panchayat = Council of five village elders!
Visual Icon: Five elders seated under a large banyan tree.

Definition: A decision on an issue in a civil or criminal case made by a judge or council.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈvɜː.dɪkt/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The Panchayat Chief delivered a wise and fair verdict.
Memory Trigger: Verdict = Final decision of justice!
Visual Icon: A wooden gavel resting on a leather block.

Definition: Guilty of or involving deceit; misleading or dishonest.
Phonetic & Usage: /dɪˈsiːt.fəl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The deceitful neighbour claimed he sold the well structure, but not the water inside.
Memory Trigger: Deceitful = Dishonest and tricky!
Visual Icon: A fox face icon symbolizing cunning deceit.

Definition: A deep shaft or hole sunk into the earth to obtain water.
Phonetic & Usage: /wɛl/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The poor farmer bought a deep stone well from his neighbour.
Memory Trigger: Well = Deep water source in the ground!
Visual Icon: A circular stone well with a bucket and rope pulley.

Definition: Keeping something in a location until needed.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈstɔː.rɪdʒ/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The Chief ruled that storing water inside another man's well requires rent.
Memory Trigger: Storage = Storing items in a space!
Visual Icon: Water inside a stone well structure.

Definition: A tenant's regular payment to a landlord for the use of property.
Phonetic & Usage: /rɛnt/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: If you store your water in his well, you must pay daily rent!
Memory Trigger: Rent = Payment for using someone's space!
Visual Icon: A coin pouch handed over a table.

Definition: Just behavior or treatment; fairness and truth in law.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈdʒʌs.tɪs/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The Panchayati Raj system ensures accessible justice for villagers.
Memory Trigger: Justice = Fair and equal treatment for all!
Visual Icon: A balanced scale of justice icon.

Definition: A group of houses and associated buildings in a rural area.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈvɪl.ɪdʒ/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The dispute occurred in a peaceful rural village.
Memory Trigger: Village = Rural community neighborhood!
Visual Icon: Cluster of thatched roof houses surrounded by green fields.

Definition: The leader or head of an organization, council, or tribe.
Phonetic & Usage: /tʃiːf/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The Panchayat Chief listened patiently to both sides before speaking.
Memory Trigger: Chief = Head of the council!
Visual Icon: An elder wearing a traditional turban and shawl.

Definition: A disagreement, argument, or debate between two parties.
Phonetic & Usage: /dɪˈspjuːt/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: A dispute arose over ownership of the water in the well.
Memory Trigger: Dispute = Conflict between two people!
Visual Icon: Two figures arguing over a well illustration.

Definition: Free of deceit and untruthfulness; sincere and fair.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɒn.ɪst/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The honest farmer trusted his neighbour and paid the full price.
Memory Trigger: Honest = Truthful and sincere!
Visual Icon: A hand placed over an open heart.

Definition: An assertion that something is true or belongs to oneself.
Phonetic & Usage: /kleɪm/ (Noun / Verb).
Textbook Context: The neighbour made a false claim to demand more money.
Memory Trigger: Claim = Asserting ownership!
Visual Icon: A figure pointing to a well claiming 'MINE!'.

Definition: Synonym for honest: Truthful, sincere, upright, or candid.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɒn.ɪst/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The honest (truthful) farmer told the entire story.
Memory Trigger: Honest and truthful describe sincere people!
Visual Icon: A glowing heart icon.

Definition: Antonym for deceitful: Sincere, honest, frank, or trustworthy.
Phonetic & Usage: /dɪˈsiːt.fəl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The farmer was sincere, while his neighbour was deceitful.
Memory Trigger: Deceitful lies; Sincere tells truth!
Visual Icon: A straight path next to a winding crooked path.

Definition: Synonym for verdict: Judgment, decision, ruling, or decree.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈvɜː.dɪkt/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The Panchayat gave its final verdict (ruling).
Memory Trigger: Verdict and ruling both mean legal decisions!
Visual Icon: A gavel resting on a book.

Definition: Antonym for justice: Injustice, unfairness, or partiality.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈdʒʌs.tɪs/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The Panchayat prevents injustice in the village.
Memory Trigger: Justice is fair; Injustice cheats!
Visual Icon: A balanced scale vs a tipped unbalanced scale.

Definition: Antonym for wise: Foolish, ignorant, or senseless.
Phonetic & Usage: /waɪz/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The wise Chief exposed the foolish greed of the neighbour.
Memory Trigger: Wise thinks deeply; Foolish acts blindly!
Visual Icon: An owl beside a silly jester hat.

Definition: Antonym for poor: Wealthy, rich, or prosperous.
Phonetic & Usage: /pʊər/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The poor farmer saved for years to buy a well.
Memory Trigger: Poor has little; Rich has much!
Visual Icon: An empty coin pouch next to a full gold chest.

Definition: Synonym for claim: Demand, assert, allege, or insist.
Phonetic & Usage: /kleɪm/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: His claim (demand) was rejected by the Chief.
Memory Trigger: Claim and demand assert ownership!
Visual Icon: A hand reaching out to grab a key.

Definition: Antonym for legal: Illegal, unlawful, or illicit.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈliː.ɡəl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Withholding water after selling a well is illegal.
Memory Trigger: Legal obeys rules; Illegal breaks laws!
Visual Icon: A green checkmark next to a red stop sign.

Definition: Antonym for clear: Vague, ambiguous, or confusing.
Phonetic & Usage: /klɪər/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The Chief gave a clear ruling without any confusion.
Memory Trigger: Clear is obvious; Vague is confusing!
Visual Icon: A clear sun icon next to a foggy cloud.

Definition: Antonym for unity: Division, discord, or conflict.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈjuː.nə.ti/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Fair verdicts restore harmony and unity in the village.
Memory Trigger: Unity joins together; Division splits apart!
Visual Icon: Hands linked together in a circle.

Definition: The letter 'h' is silent at the start of honest, hour, honor, heir.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɒn.ɪst/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: An honest (/ˈɒn.ɪst/) farmer bought the well.
Memory Trigger: H is silent in honest!
Visual Icon: A heart badge with silent 'H' crossed out.

Definition: The letter 'g' is silent before 'n' in design, sign, campaign.
Phonetic & Usage: /dɪˈzaɪn/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The deceitful neighbour hid a greedy design.
Memory Trigger: G is silent in design!
Visual Icon: A blueprint paper with muted 'G'.

Definition: The letter 'c' before 'i' in decision makes a soft /s/ sound.
Phonetic & Usage: /dɪˈsɪʒ.ən/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The Panchayat reached a unanimous decision (/s/).
Memory Trigger: C before I says soft /s/!
Visual Icon: A gavel with soft 'S' sound wave.

Definition: The digraph 'ch' makes a /tʃ/ sound in chief, chair, choice.
Phonetic & Usage: /tʃiːf/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The Panchayat Chief (/tʃ/) spoke wisely.
Memory Trigger: CH says /tʃ/ like chest!
Visual Icon: An elder turban icon with 'CH -> /tʃ/'.

Definition: The vowel pair 'oi' makes an /ɔɪ/ sound in choice, noise, voice.
Phonetic & Usage: /tʃɔɪs/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The neighbour made a greedy choice (/ɔɪ/).
Memory Trigger: OI says /ɔɪ/ like coin!
Visual Icon: Two arrows pointing to choice paths.

Definition: The letter 't' is silent in fasten, listen, glisten, castle.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈfɑː.sən/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Fasten the rope bucket to draw well water.
Memory Trigger: T sleeps in fasten!
Visual Icon: A rope knot with muted 'T'.

Definition: The letter 'w' is silent before 'r' in wrong, write, wrist.
Phonetic & Usage: /rɒŋ/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Greedy trickery is always wrong.
Memory Trigger: W rests before R in wrong!
Visual Icon: A red X over a silent 'W'.

Definition: The letter 'k' is silent before 'n' in knight, know, knee.
Phonetic & Usage: /naɪt/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Justice protects the poor like a noble knight.
Memory Trigger: K is quiet in knight!
Visual Icon: A shield with silent 'K'.

Definition: Building words using suffixes: deceit + ful = deceitful; care + less = careless; judge + ment = judgment.
Phonetic & Usage: Suffix Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: A deceitful man acts without care and receives poor judgment.
Memory Trigger: Suffixes change word meanings and grammar classes!
Visual Icon: Root word puzzle pieces adding suffix blocks.

Definition: Expressing hypothetical conditions and results using 'If... then...' structures.
Phonetic & Usage: Grammar Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: If you own the water inside, THEN pay rent for storing it in his well!
Memory Trigger: IF sets condition; THEN gives result!
Visual Icon: Flowchart arrows: IF Condition -> THEN Outcome.

flashcards.front_content: Direct & Indirect Quotes in Legal Logic
flashcards.back_content:
Definition: Reporting statements directly with quotation marks or indirectly as reported logic.
Phonetic & Usage: Grammar Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: He said, 'I sold the well, not the water.' / He claimed that he had sold the well.
Memory Trigger: Quotes capture exact spoken testimony!
Visual Icon: Two speech bubbles comparing direct vs reported quotes.

Definition: Forming past perfect verbs using had + past participle to denote an event completed prior to another past action.
Phonetic & Usage: Tense Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: The farmer HAD PAID full money before the neighbour made his claim.
Memory Trigger: HAD + V3 = Action completed BEFORE another past event!
Visual Icon: A timeline showing Event 1 (had paid) before Event 2 (claimed).

Definition: Nouns representing intangible virtues or vices (truth, deceit, justice, greed, wisdom).
Phonetic & Usage: Noun Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Truth and justice prevail over greed and deceit.
Memory Trigger: Moral qualities are abstract nouns!
Visual Icon: A heart, scale, and lightbulb grouped together.

Definition: Connecting contrasting ideas using words like 'however', 'but', 'yet'.
Phonetic & Usage: Conjunction Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: He bought the well; HOWEVER, the neighbour refused water access.
Memory Trigger: 'However' signals a turn or contrast!
Visual Icon: A road split with a 'HOWEVER' signpost.

Definition: Using 'must' to state mandatory legal or moral requirements.
Phonetic & Usage: Verb Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: You MUST remove your water or pay daily rent immediately!
Memory Trigger: MUST states mandatory orders!
Visual Icon: A red stop sign with 'MUST' text.

Definition: Biographical EVS integration: Sri Ramakrishna taught that truth and kindness unite all human beings.
Phonetic & Usage: Values Integration (General Knowledge).
Textbook Context: Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa inspired truth and selfless harmony.
Memory Trigger: Truth unites all people in peace!
Visual Icon: A glowing lotus icon representing harmony.

Definition: Didn't is the contraction for 'did not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈdɪd.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: The neighbour didn't expect such a clever verdict.
Memory Trigger: Didn't = Did + Not!
Visual Icon: A surprised face icon.

Definition: Wouldn't is the contraction for 'would not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈwʊd.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: He wouldn't pay rent, so he removed his water.
Memory Trigger: Wouldn't = Would + Not!
Visual Icon: A hand waving 'no'.

Definition: Couldn't is the contraction for 'could not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈkʊd.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: The greedy neighbour couldn't refute the Chief's logic.
Memory Trigger: Couldn't = Could + Not!
Visual Icon: A puzzle piece that doesn't fit.

Definition: He'd stands for 'he had' or 'he would'.
Phonetic & Usage: /hiːd/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: He'd paid the full price for the stone well.
Memory Trigger: He'd = He + Had!
Visual Icon: A coin exchange graphic.

Definition: You've is the contraction for 'you have'.
Phonetic & Usage: /juːv/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: You've sold the well, so you cannot keep your water there.
Memory Trigger: You've = You + Have!
Visual Icon: A pointer finger indicating 'you'.

Definition: Haven't is the contraction for 'have not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈhæv.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: They haven't seen a wiser verdict in the village.
Memory Trigger: Haven't = Have + Not!
Visual Icon: An open scale of justice.

Definition: Uncover or reveal dishonest trickery and hidden motives.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The Panchayat Chief's clever logic exposed the neighbour's deceit.
Memory Trigger: Expose deceit = Shine light on lies!
Visual Icon: A flashlight shining on a fox mask.

Definition: Defeated in argument through superior reasoning and truth.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The greedy man was completely outwitted by legal logic.
Memory Trigger: Outwitted by logic = Trapped by truth!
Visual Icon: A chess piece checkmating another.

Definition: Pay a regular fee for using someone else's space or property.
Phonetic & Usage: Common Phrase (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Either remove your water or pay rent to the farmer!
Memory Trigger: Pay rent = Fee for room storage!
Visual Icon: Coins placed on a table.

Definition: Fairness and truth have prevailed in a dispute.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Loud cheers rang out when justice was served.
Memory Trigger: Justice is served = Truth wins!
Visual Icon: A gavel resting peacefully on a block.

Definition: Refuse to yield or back down when facing unfair treatment.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The honest farmer stood his ground and sought the Panchayat.
Memory Trigger: Stand your ground = Hold firm for truth!
Visual Icon: A shield anchored firmly in soil.

Definition: Accept reality and truth rather than persisting in falsehood.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The neighbour was forced to face the truth and give up his claim.
Memory Trigger: Face the truth = Accept reality!
Visual Icon: A person looking into a clear mirror.

flashcards.back_content:
Definition: A person's trade, profession, or principal occupation.
Phonetic & Usage: /voʊˈkeɪ.ʃən/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Rabindranath Tagore's poem explores various daily vocations.
Memory Trigger: Vocation = Your daily work or trade!
Visual Icon: Icons of a hammer, spade, and lantern combined.

Definition: A person who travels about selling goods, typically calling out in the street.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈhɔː.kər/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: At 10 AM, the schoolchild meets a hawker crying, 'Bangles, crystal bangles!'
Memory Trigger: Hawkers call out their wares on the road!
Visual Icon: A street vendor carrying a tray of shiny bangles.

Definition: A sharp-edged tool for digging or cutting soil.
Phonetic & Usage: /speɪd/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: At 4 PM, the gardener digs the garden soil with his spade.
Memory Trigger: Spade = Digging shovel tool!
Visual Icon: A metal spade digging into brown garden earth.

Definition: A lamp with a transparent case protecting a flame or bulb, carried outdoors.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈlæn.tərn/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: At night, the watchman walks the alley swinging his glowing lantern.
Memory Trigger: Lantern = Portable night light!
Visual Icon: A vintage glass lantern emitting a warm yellow glow.

Definition: A formal expression of disapproval or scolding.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈrɛp.rɪ.mɑːnd/ (Noun / Verb).
Textbook Context: Nobody takes the gardener to task or gives him a reprimand if he soils his clothes.
Memory Trigger: Reprimand = Getting scolded for messy clothes!
Visual Icon: An adult pointing a scolding finger.

Definition: A dark shape produced by a body coming between rays of light and a surface.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈʃæd.oʊ/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The watchman walks all night chasing his own long shadow.
Memory Trigger: Shadow follows light everywhere!
Visual Icon: A figure walking with a long dark shadow cast on a wall.

Definition: The state or situation of being alone, often peacefully.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈsɒl.ɪ.tjuːd/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The watchman walks in peaceful solitude down the quiet lane.
Memory Trigger: Solitude = Quiet peaceful alone time!
Visual Icon: A single figure walking under starry night skies.

Definition: Freedom from outside control or fixed schedules.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˌɪn.dɪˈpɛn.dəns/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The young child yearns for the unrestricted independence of outdoor workers.
Memory Trigger: Independence = Freedom to choose your path!
Visual Icon: A bird flying out of an open cage door.

Definition: The state or quality of being worthy of honor and respect.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈdɪɡ.nə.ti/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Tagore's poem celebrates the dignity of labor in all professions.
Memory Trigger: Dignity = Every honest job deserves respect!
Visual Icon: A golden crown over working tools.

Definition: Pursuing or following rapidly.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈtʃeɪ.sɪŋ/ (Verb).
Textbook Context: The watchman walks with his lantern, chasing shadows down the alley.
Memory Trigger: Chasing = Running after something!
Visual Icon: A figure walking fast behind a trailing shadow.

Definition: A narrow passageway between buildings.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈæl.i/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The street-lamp stands like a giant in the dark lonely alley.
Memory Trigger: Alley = Narrow lane between houses!
Visual Icon: A narrow street lined with brick walls under a streetlamp.

Definition: Clear, transparent glass or mineral of high quality.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈkrɪs.təl/ (Adjective / Noun).
Textbook Context: The hawker sells beautiful crystal bangles that sparkle in sunlight.
Memory Trigger: Crystal = Clear sparkling glass!
Visual Icon: Sparkling clear glass bangles reflecting light.

Definition: Synonym for vocation: Occupation, profession, trade, or calling.
Phonetic & Usage: /voʊˈkeɪ.ʃən/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Every vocation (profession) contributes to society.
Memory Trigger: Vocation and profession mean daily work!
Visual Icon: A toolbox containing diverse tools.

Definition: Synonym for solitude: Loneliness, seclusion, isolation, or quiet.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈsɒl.ɪ.tjuːd/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The watchman walked in quiet solitude (seclusion).
Memory Trigger: Solitude and seclusion mean quiet alone time!
Visual Icon: A single lantern under a starry sky.

Definition: Antonym for freedom: Constraint, restriction, or obligation.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈfriː.dəm/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The child felt restricted by school time, but wanted freedom.
Memory Trigger: Freedom is unconstrained; Restriction binds!
Visual Icon: A clock face with locked chains.

Definition: Antonym for dark: Bright, luminous, or radiant.
Phonetic & Usage: /dɑːk/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The lantern lit up the dark alley with bright light.
Memory Trigger: Dark lacks light; Bright glows!
Visual Icon: A glowing lightbulb next to a dark shadow.

Definition: Antonym for soft: Harsh, rough, or loud.
Phonetic & Usage: /sɒft/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The mother's scolding was harsh, but the night was soft.
Memory Trigger: Soft yields; Harsh presses hard!
Visual Icon: A gentle feather beside a rough stone.

Definition: Antonym for unrestricted: Bound, restricted, or scheduled.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˌʌn.rɪˈstrɪk.tɪd/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Hawkers lead an unrestricted life, while schoolkids follow schedules.
Memory Trigger: Unrestricted is free; Scheduled is fixed!
Visual Icon: An open road vs a ticking clock.

Definition: Antonym for busy: Idle, quiet, or inactive.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈbɪz.i/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The morning street was busy, but the night alley was quiet.
Memory Trigger: Busy hums with action; Idle stays still!
Visual Icon: A bustling market next to a sleeping lane.

Definition: Antonym for quiet: Noisy, loud, or boisterous.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈkwaɪ.ət/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The gardener worked in quiet peace away from noisy streets.
Memory Trigger: Quiet is peaceful; Noisy is loud!
Visual Icon: A quiet flower garden next to a booming speaker.

Definition: Antonym for innocent: Guileful, worldly, or mischievous.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɪn.ə.sənt/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: The child's wish was pure and innocent.
Memory Trigger: Innocent has no guile; Worldly knows craft!
Visual Icon: A child smiling innocently.

Definition: Synonym for honor: Respect, dignity, or esteem.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɒn.ər/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: All working trades carry honor (respect).
Memory Trigger: Honor and dignity describe noble work!
Visual Icon: A golden medal badge.

Definition: The letter cluster 'gh' is silent in night, light, bright, sight.
Phonetic & Usage: /naɪt/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: At night (/naɪt/), the watchman walks with his lantern.
Memory Trigger: GH stays silent in night!
Visual Icon: A crescent moon with silent 'GH' crossed out.

Definition: The letter 'w' is silent in word endings like shadow, window, yellow.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈʃæd.oʊ/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: He walks chasing his long shadow (/ˈʃæd.oʊ/).
Memory Trigger: W is quiet at the end of shadow!
Visual Icon: A shadow figure with ghosted 'W'.

Definition: The letter 'c' before 'a' makes a hard /k/ sound, but '-tion' makes a soft /ʃən/ sound.
Phonetic & Usage: /voʊˈkeɪ.ʃən/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Say vo-CA-tion with soft '-tion' ending.
Memory Trigger: '-tion' says /ʃən/ like station!
Visual Icon: A word block showing '-tion' -> /ʃən/.

Definition: The vowel blend 'aw' in hawker makes an /ɔː/ sound as in saw, lawn, hawk.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈhɔː.kər/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The hawker (/ˈhɔː.kər/) cried 'Bangles!'
Memory Trigger: AW says /ɔː/ like hawk!
Visual Icon: A street vendor icon with 'AW' highlighted.

Definition: The vowel 'i' in giant makes a long /aɪ/ sound.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈdʒaɪ.ənt/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The streetlamp stands like a giant (/ˈdʒaɪ.ənt/).
Memory Trigger: Giant starts with soft 'g' and long 'i'!
Visual Icon: A giant streetlamp figure.

Definition: The letter 'l' is silent in walk, talk, chalk, stalk.
Phonetic & Usage: /wɔːk/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: I walk to school every morning at ten.
Memory Trigger: L sleeps when you walk!
Visual Icon: A walking shoe with silent 'L'.

Definition: The letter 'k' is silent before 'n' in knowledge, know, knee.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈnɒl.ɪdʒ/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: A child gathers knowledge from observing daily life.
Memory Trigger: K is quiet before N!
Visual Icon: An open book with silent 'K'.

Definition: The letter 'b' is silent after 'm' in thumb, limb, comb.
Phonetic & Usage: /θʌm/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: The gardener had dirt on his thumb.
Memory Trigger: B is quiet after M!
Visual Icon: A thumb icon with silent 'B'.

Definition: A figure of speech comparing two unlike things using 'like' or 'as' (stands like a giant with one red eye).
Phonetic & Usage: Literary Device (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: The street-lamp stands LIKE a giant with one red eye.
Memory Trigger: Similes use 'LIKE' or 'AS' to make vivid pictures!
Visual Icon: A streetlamp drawn as a giant holding a red glowing eye.

flashcards.front_content: Subjunctive Wishes: I wish I were
flashcards.back_content:
Definition: Using 'I wish I were...' to express imaginary or unfulfilled desires.
Phonetic & Usage: Grammar Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: I wish I were a hawker spending my day on the road!
Memory Trigger: 'I wish I WERE' expresses imagined dream roles!
Visual Icon: A child with a thought bubble showing a hawker tray.

Definition: Prepositions showing directional travel (through the lane, past the gate, down the alley).
Phonetic & Usage: Preposition Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: He walks past the gate and down the dark alley.
Memory Trigger: Prepositions move the story through space!
Visual Icon: A path arrow moving PAST a gate DOWN a lane.

Definition: Time phrases ordering events through the day (at ten in the morning, at four in the afternoon, at night).
Phonetic & Usage: Grammar Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: At ten I walk to school; at four I return; at night I look from my window.
Memory Trigger: Time connectives build a daily timeline!
Visual Icon: A clock face showing 10 AM, 4 PM, and 9 PM.

Definition: Adjectives describing sights, sounds, and textures (crystal, red, lonely, baked, dark).
Phonetic & Usage: Adjective Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Crystal bangles, red eye, lonely street, dark alley.
Memory Trigger: Sensory adjectives bring poems to life!
Visual Icon: An eye, ear, and hand icon grouped together.

Definition: Capitalizing the full name of India's Nobel laureate poet.
Phonetic & Usage: Punctuation Rule (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Rabindranath Tagore composed 'Vocation'.
Memory Trigger: Capitalize famous author names!
Visual Icon: A portrait outline of Rabindranath Tagore.

Definition: Verbs describing occupational labor (digs, sells, walks, swings, soils).
Phonetic & Usage: Verb Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: The gardener digs soil and the watchman swings his lantern.
Memory Trigger: Occupational verbs show what workers DO!
Visual Icon: A spade, tray, and lantern icon.

Definition: Expressing heartfelt wishes through exclamatory poetic lines.
Phonetic & Usage: Sentence Type (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: I wish I were a gardener with nobody to stop me from digging!
Memory Trigger: Exclamations share deep wishes!
Visual Icon: A starburst speech bubble with a wish.

Definition: I'd stands for 'I would' or 'I had'.
Phonetic & Usage: /aɪd/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: I'd spend all my day on the road crying 'Bangles!'
Memory Trigger: I'd = I + Would!
Visual Icon: A child pointing to himself.

Definition: I'm is the contraction for 'I am'.
Phonetic & Usage: /aɪm/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: I'm walking to school every morning at ten.
Memory Trigger: I'm = I + Am!
Visual Icon: A schoolchild carrying a bag.

Definition: There's is the contraction for 'there is'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ðɛəz/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: There's nobody to take the gardener to task.
Memory Trigger: There's = There + Is!
Visual Icon: A gardener digging happily.

Definition: Wouldn't is the contraction for 'would not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈwʊd.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: Nobody wouldn't scold him if he gets baked in the sun.
Memory Trigger: Wouldn't = Would + Not!
Visual Icon: A sun shining brightly.

Definition: Can't is the contraction for 'cannot'.
Phonetic & Usage: /kɑːnt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: A child can't stay out all night without scolding.
Memory Trigger: Can't = Can + Not!
Visual Icon: A bedroom window at night.

Definition: She'll is the contraction for 'she will'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ʃiːl/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: She'll put me to bed when night comes.
Memory Trigger: She'll = She + Will!
Visual Icon: A mother putting a child to bed.

Definition: The philosophy that all honest jobs deserve equal respect and value.
Phonetic & Usage: Ethical Concept (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Tagore's Vocation teaches the dignity of labor for all workers.
Memory Trigger: Dignity of labor = Every job is honorable!
Visual Icon: A spade, lantern, and book grouped under a crown.

Definition: Pursue imaginary or elusive goals that cannot be caught.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The watchman walks all night, chasing shadows down the lane.
Memory Trigger: Chase shadows = Follow dark shapes in the night!
Visual Icon: A figure running after a long shadow.

flashcards.front_content: Grass is greener on the other side
flashcards.back_content:
Definition: Other people's lives or jobs always seem better or freer than our own.
Phonetic & Usage: Proverb / Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The child thinks the grass is greener on the gardener's side.
Memory Trigger: Grass is greener = Others' jobs look easier!
Visual Icon: A fence separating dry grass from lush green grass.

Definition: A fixed, predetermined path that one must follow.
Phonetic & Usage: Common Phrase (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The hawker has no set route and no fixed time to hurry home.
Memory Trigger: Set route = A fixed path to follow!
Visual Icon: A map with a straight dotted path.

Definition: Poetic imagery referring to the red glowing lamp atop a street post.
Phonetic & Usage: Poetic Phrase (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The street-lamp stands like a giant with one red eye.
Memory Trigger: One red eye = A glowing red street lamp!
Visual Icon: A tall streetlamp with a red bulb.

Definition: Completely unrestricted, unconstrained, and free to go anywhere.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The child longs to be as free as a bird on the road.
Memory Trigger: Free as a bird = Total freedom!
Visual Icon: A bird soaring high in an open sky.

flashcards.back_content:
Definition: A worker in a skilled trade, especially one that involves making things by hand.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɑː.tɪ.zæn/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Ravi is a skilled traditional glass artisan in Firozabad.
Memory Trigger: Artisan = Skilled handcrafted worker!
Visual Icon: An artisan holding a glassblowing pipe.

Definition: An enclosed structure in which material is heated to very high temperatures.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈfɜː.nɪs/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Artisans shape glowing glass near intense furnace flames.
Memory Trigger: Furnace = High-heat oven for glass!
Visual Icon: A glowing orange furnace with fire flames.

Definition: The introduction of new ideas, methods, or original products.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˌɪn.əˈveɪ.ʃən/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Ananya introduced modern floral innovations to her father's glass bangles.
Memory Trigger: Innovation = Fresh modern ideas!
Visual Icon: A glowing lightbulb sprouting flower petals.

Definition: Made liquid by heat; melted glass or metal.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈmoʊl.tən/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Ravi shapes liquid molten glass into glowing circular rings.
Memory Trigger: Molten = Melted hot liquid glass!
Visual Icon: Liquid orange glass dripping off a rod.

Definition: Valued cultural traditions passed down through generations.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈhɛr.ɪ.tɪdʒ/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Firozabad is world-famous for its traditional glassmaking heritage.
Memory Trigger: Heritage = Passed down from ancestors!
Visual Icon: An old family photo frame beside bangles.

Definition: Lit up; made bright with light or success.
Phonetic & Usage: /ɪˈluː.mɪ.neɪ.tɪd/ (Verb / Adjective).
Textbook Context: The Diwali collection illuminated the family workshop with festive success.
Memory Trigger: Illuminated = Filled with bright light!
Visual Icon: A workshop glowing with warm oil lamps.

Definition: A famous industrial city in Uttar Pradesh known as the glass city of India.
Phonetic & Usage: /fɪˈroʊ.zɑː.bɑːd/ (Proper Noun).
Textbook Context: Firozabad is the traditional center of India's glass bangle industry.
Memory Trigger: Firozabad = Glass city of India!
Visual Icon: A map pin over Uttar Pradesh reading Firozabad.

Definition: A business organization or entrepreneurial project.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɛn.tər.praɪz/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Ananya's modern designs revitalized the family enterprise.
Memory Trigger: Enterprise = A thriving business project!
Visual Icon: A storefront sign with a rising growth arrow.

Definition: The Indian festival of lights celebrating prosperity and joy.
Phonetic & Usage: /dɪˈwɑː.li/ (Proper Noun).
Textbook Context: The new floral glass bangles became a massive hit during Diwali.
Memory Trigger: Diwali = Festival of lights!
Visual Icon: Row of burning clay diyas and sparkling bangles.

Definition: Of, relating to, or decorated with flower motifs.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈflɔː.rəl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Ananya painted delicate floral patterns on the glass bangles.
Memory Trigger: Floral = Decorated with flowers!
Visual Icon: A green glass bangle with painted pink flowers.

Definition: The process of cooling liquid molten glass into a solid rigid form.
Phonetic & Usage: /səˌlɪd.ɪ.fɪˈkeɪ.ʃən/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Rapid solidification sets the circular shape of glass bangles.
Memory Trigger: Solidification = Liquid turning solid!
Visual Icon: Liquid glass cooling into a solid ring.

Definition: The detailed organization and transport of goods from producer to market.
Phonetic & Usage: /ləˈdʒɪs.tɪks/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Increased bangle orders boosted local packaging and transport logistics.
Memory Trigger: Logistics = Moving goods to market!
Visual Icon: A delivery truck loaded with boxed packages.

Definition: Synonym for innovation: Modernization, novelty, invention, or reform.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˌɪn.əˈveɪ.ʃən/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Her design innovation (modernization) boosted sales.
Memory Trigger: Innovation and modernization mean new ideas!
Visual Icon: A lightbulb bursting with creative ideas.

Definition: Synonym for molten: Liquefied, melted, fused, or fluid.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈmoʊl.tən/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Liquid molten (melted) glass glows orange.
Memory Trigger: Molten and melted describe liquid state!
Visual Icon: A drop of liquid orange glass.

Definition: Synonym for illuminated: Lit up, brightened, radiant, or glowing.
Phonetic & Usage: /ɪˈluː.mɪ.neɪ.tɪd/ (Verb).
Textbook Context: Festival diyas illuminated (lit up) the room.
Memory Trigger: Illuminated and lit up mean glowing bright!
Visual Icon: A glowing diya lamp emitting rays.

Definition: Antonym for traditional: Modern, contemporary, or innovative.
Phonetic & Usage: /trəˈdɪʃ.ən.əl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: She combined traditional crafts with modern designs.
Memory Trigger: Traditional is old; Modern is fresh!
Visual Icon: An old wooden loom next to a digital tablet.

Definition: Antonym for success: Failure, defeat, or setback.
Phonetic & Usage: /səkˈsɛs/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: The Diwali sale was a great success rather than a failure.
Memory Trigger: Success triumphs; Failure falls short!
Visual Icon: A rising growth chart vs a falling line.

Definition: Antonym for expand: Shrink, contract, or reduce.
Phonetic & Usage: /ɪkˈspænd/ (Verb).
Textbook Context: New orders caused the workshop to expand.
Memory Trigger: Expand grows bigger; Shrink gets smaller!
Visual Icon: An expanding circle arrow.

Definition: Antonym for educated: Unlettered, uneducated, or ignorant.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɛdʒ.ʊ.keɪ.tɪd/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Ananya was an educated young woman with fresh skills.
Memory Trigger: Educated gains knowledge; Unlettered lacks schooling!
Visual Icon: A graduation cap beside an open book.

Definition: Antonym for bright: Dull, dim, or faded.
Phonetic & Usage: /braɪt/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Vibrant bright bangles attract buyers better than dull ones.
Memory Trigger: Bright shines vividly; Dull looks faded!
Visual Icon: A gleaming gold bangle next to a faded gray ring.

Definition: Antonym for malleable: Rigid, stiff, brittle, or unyielding.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈmæl.i.ə.bəl/ (Adjective).
Textbook Context: Hot glass is malleable, but cold glass is rigid and brittle.
Memory Trigger: Malleable bends; Rigid snaps!
Visual Icon: A bendable wire next to a stiff glass rod.

Definition: Synonym for prosperity: Wealth, success, affluence, or growth.
Phonetic & Usage: /prɒsˈpɛr.ə.ti/ (Noun).
Textbook Context: Diwali sales brought financial prosperity (growth).
Memory Trigger: Prosperity and wealth mean thriving success!
Visual Icon: A flourishing tree bearing gold coin fruits.

Definition: The letter 'g' is silent in design, sign, campaign, align.
Phonetic & Usage: /dɪˈzaɪn/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Ananya introduced a fresh floral design (/dɪˈzaɪn/).
Memory Trigger: G is silent in design!
Visual Icon: A sketchpad with silent 'G' crossed out.

Definition: The final 'e' in furnace is silent, giving a soft /s/ sound to 'c'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈfɜː.nɪs/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Molten glass heats in the furnace (/ˈfɜː.nɪs/).
Memory Trigger: Final E stays quiet in furnace!
Visual Icon: A furnace fire with silent 'E'.

Definition: Words with three syllables like 'ar-ti-san' stress the first syllable.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɑː.tɪ.zæn/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Say AR-ti-san with primary stress on AR.
Memory Trigger: Break it: AR - TI - SAN!
Visual Icon: Three sound blocks with the first block highlighted.

Definition: The letter 'c' before 'i' in city makes a soft /s/ sound.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈsɪt.i/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Frozabad is the glass city (/s/) of India.
Memory Trigger: C before I says soft /s/!
Visual Icon: A city skyline with soft 'S' icon.

Definition: The noun suffix '-tion' is pronounced as /ʃən/ in innovation, solidication.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˌɪn.əˈveɪ.ʃən/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Floral innovation (/ʃən/) brought business growth.
Memory Trigger: '-tion' says /ʃən/ like station!
Visual Icon: A word puzzle showing '-tion' -> /ʃən/.

Definition: The vowel 'i' in Diwali makes a long /iː/ sound.
Phonetic & Usage: /dɪˈwɑː.li/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: They sold floral bangles for Diwali (/dɪˈwɑː.li/).
Memory Trigger: Diwali has long /iː/ sounds!
Visual Icon: A burning diya lamp with 'Diwali' text.

Definition: The letter 'k' is silent before 'n' in knee, know, knife.
Phonetic & Usage: /niː/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Artisans sit with glass rods on their knee.
Memory Trigger: K is silent before N!
Visual Icon: A leg joint with silent 'K'.

Definition: The letter 'h' is silent in hour, honest, honor.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈaʊ.ər/ (Phonics Rule).
Textbook Context: Ravi works many an hour near the furnace.
Memory Trigger: H stays silent in hour!
Visual Icon: A clock face with silent 'H'.

Definition: Forming past perfect verbs using HAD + past participle to show an event completed before another past action.
Phonetic & Usage: Tense Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Ananya HAD COMPLETED her studies before she joined the workshop.
Memory Trigger: HAD + V3 = Action finished BEFORE another past event!
Visual Icon: A timeline showing Event 1 (Had completed) before Event 2 (Joined).

Definition: Specific names of cities, festivals, and people requiring capital letters (Firozabad, Diwali, Ravi, Ananya).
Phonetic & Usage: Noun Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Ananya designed bangles in Firozabad for Diwali.
Memory Trigger: Specific cities and festivals get BIG capital letters!
Visual Icon: A festival banner reading 'Firozabad Diwali Collection'.

Definition: Nouns created by joining words describing manufacturing crafts (glassmaking, workshop, packaging).
Phonetic & Usage: Word Formation (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Glassmaking takes place in the family workshop.
Memory Trigger: Glass + Making = Glassmaking!
Visual Icon: Workshop icon showing tools.

Definition: Adverbs ordering manufacturing steps (first, next, then, finally).
Phonetic & Usage: Adverb Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: First heat the glass; next shape it; then paint floral motifs; finally box it.
Memory Trigger: Sequence adverbs order process steps!
Visual Icon: Step 1 -> Step 2 -> Step 3 -> Step 4.

Definition: Descriptive words highlighting artisanal qualities (molten, floral, delicate, illuminated).
Phonetic & Usage: Adjective Class (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Delicate floral patterns on molten glass bangles.
Memory Trigger: Craftsmanship adjectives describe fine details!
Visual Icon: A sparkling decorated bangle with labels.

Definition: Describing steps where the object receives the action (glass is heated, bangles are boxed).
Phonetic & Usage: Grammar Mechanics (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Glass is heated in furnaces and boxed for transport.
Memory Trigger: Passive Voice: Object + IS/ARE + V3!
Visual Icon: A factory conveyer belt process diagram.

Definition: Connecting daughter's innovation to village economic prosperity using 'because' and 'therefore'.
Phonetic & Usage: Conjunction Rule (Grammar Concept).
Textbook Context: Because Ananya created floral designs, therefore village sales doubled.
Memory Trigger: Cause leads directly to Effect!
Visual Icon: A cause arrow pointing to a growth chart.

Definition: Understanding how local art drives regional transport, packaging, and retail employment.
Phonetic & Usage: EVS Integration (General Knowledge).
Textbook Context: Bangle sales create jobs in packaging, logistics, and retail stores.
Memory Trigger: Local craft powers community growth!
Visual Icon: A chain linking furnace -> design -> truck -> store.

Definition: Hadn't is the contraction for 'had not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈhæd.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: Ravi hadn't expected such a high Diwali demand.
Memory Trigger: Hadn't = Had + Not!
Visual Icon: A surprised artisan face.

Definition: She'd stands for 'she had' or 'she would'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ʃiːd/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: She'd designed 10 floral patterns before Diwali.
Memory Trigger: She'd = She + Had!
Visual Icon: Ananya holding a sketchpad.

Definition: They'd stands for 'they had' or 'they would'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ðeɪd/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: They'd expanded the workshop to meet new orders.
Memory Trigger: They'd = They + Had!
Visual Icon: An expanded workshop building.

Definition: Couldn't is the contraction for 'could not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈkʊd.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: Traditional designs couldn't attract younger buyers alone.
Memory Trigger: Couldn't = Could + Not!
Visual Icon: An old plain bangle.

Definition: Isn't is the contraction for 'is not'.
Phonetic & Usage: /ˈɪz.ənt/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: Firozabad isn't just a city; it's a glass heritage hub.
Memory Trigger: Isn't = Is + Not!
Visual Icon: A map pin over Firozabad.

Definition: We've is the contraction for 'we have'.
Phonetic & Usage: /wiːv/ (Contraction).
Textbook Context: We've created a successful floral collection!
Memory Trigger: We've = We + Have!
Visual Icon: Ravi and Ananya celebrating.

Definition: Revitalize, modernize, or bring fresh energy to something old.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Ananya's floral designs breathed new life into the glass workshop.
Memory Trigger: Breathe new life = Revitalize with fresh energy!
Visual Icon: A blooming flower emerging from an old stump.

Definition: Working together in close cooperation and harmony.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Generational wisdom and youth innovation go hand in hand.
Memory Trigger: Hand in hand = Close cooperation!
Visual Icon: Two hands joined together.

Definition: Expanding a village handicraft to reach national and international markets.
Phonetic & Usage: Economic Motto (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Firozabad glass bangles travel from local workshops to global markets.
Memory Trigger: Local to global = Village craft to world markets!
Visual Icon: A village globe surrounded by transport trucks.

Definition: A promising, successful, and prosperous future ahead.
Phonetic & Usage: Common Phrase (Phrase).
Textbook Context: Educated youth bring a bright future to traditional family crafts.
Memory Trigger: Bright future = Success and light ahead!
Visual Icon: A shining sun over a rising road.

Definition: A person, craft, or achievement that brings great honor to a village.
Phonetic & Usage: Common Phrase (Phrase).
Textbook Context: The Diwali glass bangle collection became the pride of the community.
Memory Trigger: Pride of community = Honored by all!
Visual Icon: A village trophy award.

Definition: An innovative or contemporary update added to a traditional concept.
Phonetic & Usage: Idiom (Phrase).
Textbook Context: She gave traditional glass bangles a fresh modern twist with floral motifs.
Memory Trigger: Modern twist = Fresh new style!
Visual Icon: A traditional loop with a modern spiral twist.
